item.title: Global infrastructure leaders converge in Hong Kong to drive high-quality construction developments (with photos)
item.description:
InfraEX Week 2026, spearheaded by the Development Bureau (DEVB), opened today (November 20). It brings together three major construction events, namely its flagship opening event, the 2nd International Infrastructure and Projects Leaders Summit; the International Conference on Modular Construction 2026 and the Construction Innovation Expo 2026. The Week aims to establish a premier international exchange platform to promote sustainable development, enhance efficiency in infrastructure delivery, and accelerate the adoption of innovative technologies, serving as a key catalyst for driving the upgrading and transformation of the construction industry.
      
     Speaking at the grand opening ceremony of InfraEX Week 2026, the Chief Executive, Mr John Lee, said that, in a world shaped by shifting geopolitics, urgent climate challenges and rapid technological advance, ideas must be turned into projects with lasting impact through innovation, collaboration and clear strategic direction. He went on to say that Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan provides a strategic roadmap for Hong Kong's future, giving businesses, investors and innovators strategic insight into the city's development and emerging opportunities. He cited the Northern Metropolis, which is central to the Five-Year Plan, as an example of such development and opportunities. To build the Northern Metropolis and all that it promises, he said that Hong Kong must deliver infrastructure that is truly future-ready, supported by the smart city concept, artificial intelligence, advanced engineering technologies, and innovative construction methods and materials. He stressed that, for excellence in the construction industry, collaboration is the most important factor.
      
     Mr Lee then witnessed the exchanges of a letter of intent and memoranda of understanding between the DEVB and various local and overseas institutions to foster in-depth exchanges and collaboration across regions and sectors, laying a solid foundation for more local and Mainland construction enterprises and products to "go global".
      
     Vice Minister of the Ministry of Water Resources Mr Liu Dongshun stated at the opening ceremony that the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government announced its First Five-Year Plan in September this year, setting out development goals including advancing the development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA), promoting "hard connectivity" in infrastructure, and fostering digitalisation and upgrading of infrastructure resilience, while leveraging its advantages of enjoying strong support from the motherland and being closely connected to the world to reinforce its position as an international infrastructure centre. He added that the Ministry of Water Resources will, as always, deepen exchanges and co-operation with Hong Kong for water-related affairs, providing solid water security guarantees to support the high-quality development of the GBA and safeguard the long-term prosperity and stability of Hong Kong.
      
     Held concurrently today, the 2nd International Infrastructure and Projects Leaders Summit, themed "Envisioning a Sustainable Future: From Insights to Impacts", explored strategies to address the challenges encountered by the construction industry, driving its upgrading, transformation, and high-quality development.
      
     In her welcome remarks at the luncheon of the Summit, the Secretary for Development, Ms Bernadette Linn, said that Hong Kong proactively integrates into and serves overall national development under "one country, two systems", and remains committed to fulfilling its role as a "super connector" and "super value-adder" to facilitate the internationalisation of national standards and showcase our nation's innovation and technology to the world. The Government is driving the transformation and upgrading of the construction industry towards advanced, intelligent, and high-quality development. In expediting the development of the Northern Metropolis, the Government is transforming practices across the board. Beyond streamlining the approval processes, the Government is harnessing artificial intelligence and driving the widespread adoption of advanced construction materials and technologies. In addition, she shared an update on the achievements since the first summit, including continuous improvement in international construction cost ranking. Hong Kong's construction cost ranking improved from the third most expensive globally in 2020 to the 16th this year, reflecting a significant improvement in cost control over that period.
      
     The Permanent Secretary for Development (Works), Mr Ricky Lau, said in his keynote presentation at the Summit that the Government is expediting the development of the Northern Metropolis and various major infrastructure projects, creating numerous opportunities for the construction industry. He noted that the construction industry is facing the opportunities and challenges posed by rapid technological changes, infrastructure upgrades and climate resilience, and is transitioning from traditional project delivery models towards a more industrialised, digitalised, and tech-enabled phase. Looking ahead, the industry's transformation will be driven by three core pillars: "Innovisation", "Talentisation", and "Collaborisation", promoting innovation and technology, talent training, and collaboration of various parties, thereby enabling the industry to continue to advance.
      
     More than 800 major infrastructure project leaders and experts from over 30 countries and regions around the world attended the Summit, including senior government officials from the Mainland and overseas, as well as representatives from renowned international organisations such as the International Institute for Management Development. They shared the latest infrastructure initiatives and challenges at the presentation session and four plenary sessions, the themes of which were "Northern Metropolis: Vast Opportunities in Action", "The Global Vanguard: Innovation at Scale", "Future-ready Workforce: Orchestrating a Connected Tomorrow", and "Future-proofing Cities: Resilience as New Competitiveness".
      
     The other two key events of InfraEX Week 2026, namely the International Conference on Modular Construction 2026 co-organised by the International Association for Modular Construction and the University of Hong Kong, will be held tomorrow (November 21); while the Construction Innovation Expo 2026, co-organised by the DEVB, the Centre of Science and Technology Industrial Development of the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, and the Construction Industry Council, will be held from November 23 to 25, showcasing cutting-edge construction innovations from around the globe.

item.title: Speech by FS at Hong Kong Export Credit Insurance Corporation 60th Anniversary Cocktail Reception (English only) (with photo)
item.description:
Following is the speech by the Financial Secretary, Mr Paul Chan, at the Hong Kong Export Credit Insurance Corporation (HKECIC) 60th Anniversary Cocktail Reception today (November 20):

Agnes (Chairperson of the HKECIC Advisory Board, Ms Agnes Chan), Terence (Commissioner of the HKECIC, Mr Terence Chiu), 王浩董事長 (Secretary of CPC Committee and Chairman of China Export & Credit Insurance Corporation, Mr Wang Hao), 周強副部長 (Deputy Director-General of the Economic Affairs Department and Head of the Commercial Office of the Liaison Office of the Central People's Government in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Mr Zhou Qiang), distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen,

     Good evening. It is a great pleasure to join you in celebrating the 60th anniversary of the Hong Kong Export Credit Insurance Corporation.

     Agnes has reminded us how far ECIC has come. Let me go back to where it began.

     On December 7, 1966, the then Financial Secretary introduced the Bill that created this Corporation. He also made a confession. As guardian of the public purse, he said, he had "cold feet" at the thought of $300 million of public funds being at risk.

     Sixty years on, that guarantee stands at $80 billion. I am glad to report that my feet are still warm.

     They are warm because ECIC has served Hong Kong well. The design has not changed: the Government stands behind the Corporation, and the Corporation underwrites on professional judgement and pays its own way.

     Hong Kong's exporters then were mostly small firms, selling garments, toys and plastic flowers on credit to buyers half a world away. A single unpaid invoice could put the whole business at risk. Export credit insurance gave them the confidence to say yes: to a new buyer, a new market, a larger order.

     That confidence has carried Hong Kong a long way. ECIC has insured more than $2.6 trillion of business for over 20,000 policyholders, covering more than 200 markets. And in terms of value, what was exported in the whole of 1966, Hong Kong now does it in half a day.

     Through energy shocks, financial crises and the pandemic, ECIC stood by its customers. I thank the Advisory Board, management and staff, past and present. Above all, I pay tribute to our exporters, in particular the long-standing policyholders we will honour shortly. This anniversary is yours too.

     Ladies and gentlemen, that confidence is needed just as much today. Tariffs, geopolitical conflict and shifting supply chains have made it harder to know whether a buyer is able to pay, and when. Yes, Hong Kong's exports rose by 45 per cent in the first nine months of this year, led by AI-related electronics. Yet strong headline figures do not remove the risks that individual exporters, particularly smaller firms, face with every order.

     Our aim is straightforward: no sound order should be lost because of a risk that can be shared. So the Government and ECIC have worked together in three ways.

     First, capacity: a larger guarantee, and cover for up to 95 per cent of a loss.

     Second, speed: when sweeping tariffs were announced in April last year, ECIC responded within days with cheaper pre-shipment cover and lower premiums for emerging markets.

     Third, reach: free credit checks on overseas buyers, cover that helps e-commerce merchants secure bank financing, and, since July, SME Protect Plus for sales to newer and smaller buyers.

     Exporters have responded: in the last financial year, ECIC insured a record $192 billion worth of export sales.

     Looking ahead, Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan commits us to strengthening our role as an international trade centre and reaching further into ASEAN (Association of Southeast Nations), the Middle East, Central Asia and Africa. I hope ECIC will go wherever our traders go: into new markets, and into e-commerce and services.

     And there are new traders to follow, too. More Mainland enterprises are going global through Hong Kong: the GoGlobal Task Force (Task Force on Supporting Mainland Enterprises in Going Global), of which ECIC is a member, has assisted more than 360 of them since its launch last October.

     I also hope ECIC will work even more closely with banks, so that insurance leads more readily to financing for smaller firms. And, of course, I hope it will keep the prudence and professionalism that have served it so well for 60 years.

     My warmest congratulations to ECIC on its Diamond Jubilee, and I wish you all an enjoyable evening. Thank you.

item.title: Committee on Innovation, Technology and Industry Development holds ninth meeting (with photos)
item.description:
The Secretary for Innovation, Technology and Industry, Professor Sun Dong, chaired the ninth meeting of the Committee on Innovation, Technology and Industry Development (CITID) this afternoon (November 20).

     At the meeting, members were briefed on the major development directions and policy initiatives in the First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (2026-2030) (Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan) and the Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address that were related to the purview of the Innovation, Technology and Industry Bureau. Members then provided various constructive suggestions on implementing the strategic directions outlined in Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan, particularly in areas such as expediting the development of innovation and technology (I&T) industries, advancing new industrialisation, and planning for frontier technologies. Their suggestions were conducive to the Government's efforts in enhancing the strategy in promoting the development of I&T in Hong Kong.

     Professor Sun said, "The National 15th Five-Year plan indicated clear support for Hong Kong's development into an international I&T centre. The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government proactively aligns with the national development strategies, and promulgated Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan, which sets out two major indicators for I&T development, namely striving to reach 3 per cent after 2030 for the ratio of total domestic expenditure on innovation activities to gross domestic product (GDP); and striving to reach 5.5 per cent after 2030 for the ratio of the value added of Manufacturing and New Industrialisation-related Industries to GDP. Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan also proposes that we will have basically established an international I&T centre based in the Greater Bay Area, serving the entire country and being connected to the world, after 2030. Along the directions set out in Hong Kong's First Five Year Plan, this year's Policy Address has already announced a series of key initiatives. The Government is committed to fully implementing the development blueprint outlined by Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan, as well as the specific measures of the Policy Address to lead Hong Kong's I&T development to enter a new phase."
 
     Established on March 3, 2023, the CITID advises the Government on the directions and strategies as set out in the Hong Kong Innovation and Technology Development Blueprint on promoting the development of I&T in Hong Kong, and enhances co-operation among stakeholders.

item.title: Hong Kong Customs shuts down drug manufacturing centre and drug repacking distribution centre with suspected drugs worth about $1.6 million seized (with photos)
item.description:
Hong Kong Customs yesterday (November 19) shut down a suspected drug repacking distribution centre in Tuen Mun and a suspected drug manufacturing centre in Tsuen Wan, seizing about 3.7 kilograms of suspected cannabis buds, 3.6kg of suspected cannabis oil, about 24kg of cannabis-infused candies and 1 148 suspected cannabis oil vape capsules, and a batch of suspected drug packaging and manufacturing paraphernalia. The total estimated market value was about $1.6 million. Three persons were arrested.

     Through intelligence analysis and in-depth investigation, Customs took enforcement actions against two targeted men. Customs officers escorted a 23-year-old targeted man and a 28-year-old woman who accompanied him to a residential flat in Tuen Mun for a search and found about 3.7kg of suspected cannabis buds, 332 suspected cannabis oil vape capsules, about 180 grams of cannabis-infused candies and a batch of drug packaging paraphernalia. Customs officers later escorted a 33-year-old targeted man to a hotel room in Tsuen Wan for a search and found about 3.6kg of suspected cannabis oil, 816 suspected cannabis oil vape capsules, about 24kg of cannabis-infused candies and a batch of drug packaging and manufacturing paraphernalia.

     The 23-year-old arrested man and 28-year-old arrested woman were charged with two counts of trafficking in a dangerous drug. The 33-year-old arrested man was charged with two counts of trafficking in a dangerous drug and one count of manufacture of a dangerous drug. The case will appear at the Shatin Magistrates' Courts tomorrow (November 21).  

     Under the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, trafficking in a dangerous drug is a serious offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $5 million and life imprisonment. 

     Members of the public may report any suspected drug trafficking activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account (crimereport@customs.gov.hk) or online form (eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002).

item.title: Speech by USCST at opening ceremony of deTour 2026 Design Festival (English only)
item.description:
Following is the speech by the Under Secretary for Culture, Sports and Tourism, Mr Raistlin Lau, at the opening ceremony of deTour 2026 Design Festival today (November 20):

Mrs Lo (Chairman of PMQ Board of Directors, Mrs Lo Lee Oi-lin), William (Executive Director of PMQ, Mr William To), Shin (curator-at-large of deTour 2026, Ms Shin Wong), curators, designers, distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen,

     Good evening. It is my great pleasure to join you all at the opening ceremony of deTour 2026 Design Festival.

     Sponsored by the Cultural and Creative Industries Development Agency under the Culture, Sports and Tourism Bureau, deTour has established itself as one of Hong Kong's annual flagship design events and serves as an important platform for showcasing the ideas and creativity of local and international talent. Since its launch in 2014, deTour has welcomed more than 1.3 million visitors and engaged over 220 design units from Hong Kong and beyond - a testament to its growing influence and popularity in the global design community.

     Under the theme, "BETTER, NOT PERFECT: Prototypes for Tomorrow", deTour 2026 tells us design is an evolving process. It is defined not by the pursuit of perfection, but by the willingness to rethink, refine, and improve upon what came before. It resonates deeply with Hong Kong's spirit - a city characterised by adaptability, resilience, and perseverance.

     Over the next 10 days, until November 29, deTour 2026 presents 14 pioneering works by creators from Hong Kong, the Chinese Mainland, and overseas across three curated zones: the Concept Lab, the IRL Field and the Future Track. From reinterpreting local neon craft into contemporary jewellery to transforming urban waste into sustainable art, these works invite us to see design as an ongoing conversation connecting people, places and possibilities.

     This year, deTour introduces its first pop-up shop, featuring limited-edition products, lifestyle items and festival merchandise by local and international designers. I have made a lot of purchases already, so it is your turn. Together with the workshops, "Creative Voice" dialogues and guided tours, deTour 2026 provides a great opportunity for everyone to explore how design can be seamlessly integrated into daily life and brings an all-round immersive experience to all of us. 

     In closing, I would like to express my gratitude to PMQ, Shin and the curatorial team for presenting such an inspiring deTour for yet another successful year. May I wish deTour 2026 a resounding success, and everyone here a fruitful and enjoyable evening. Thank you.

item.title: Civil Service College holds first seminar in Executive Series on Governance in the Age of Multilateralism (with photos)
item.description:
The Civil Service College (CSC) launched the Executive Series on Governance in the Age of Multilateralism. The first seminar on the topic of "Geopolitics and Regional Dynamics in Asia" was delivered by former Minister for Foreign Affairs of Singapore Mr George Yeo and moderated by Assistant Professor in Philosophy of University of Hong Kong Dr Brian Wong at the CSC today (November 20).

     Addressing the seminar, the Head of the CSC, Mr Oscar Kwok, said that in an era of profound transformation in geopolitical order, economies are intertwined and no country can prosper in isolation. As an international financial centre, a global trading hub and a gateway of strategic importance, Hong Kong is uniquely positioned to facilitate dialogue across different systems and host trusted platforms for multilateral co-operation and dispute resolution.

     More than 220 civil servants in directorate, senior and middle ranks from 59 bureaux/departments attended the seminar in person or online today.

     The Executive Series on Governance in the Age of Multilateralism brings together eminent global, regional and local leaders to share their insights, experiences and foresight. Through intellectual engagement and discussions, it aims to foster holistic thinking, deepen cross-cultural understanding and strengthen the shared commitment to good governance among civil servants.

item.title: Hong Kong Visual Arts Centre organises "vA!Greenery" exhibition to explore coexistence of natural surroundings and digital technology (with photos)
item.description:
The Hong Kong Visual Arts Centre (vA!) is organising the "vA!Greenery" exhibition from today (November 20), showcasing 3D-printed sculptural installations by artists Tse Yim-on and Wong Tin-hang that transform observations of nature and artistic imaginings to explore possibilities for the coexistence of nature and the artificial, as well as the relationship between art and technology.
 
     Tse and Wong have taken the banyan stump near the entrance of vA! as the starting point for their creations. Drawing inspiration from the plant forms, natural surroundings and urban memories of Hong Kong Park, they transform observations of nature and artistic imaginings into 3D-printed sculptural installations that unfold across various levels of vA!. The artworks combine painting, AI-assisted generation, digital modelling and 3D printing, interweaving the vivid colours and imagined plants in Tse's paintings with forms developed by Wong through botanical observation and digital techniques, taking viewers to discover the creative possibilities that emerge through the meeting of art and AI.
 
     The exhibition is presented by the Leisure and Cultural Services Department and organised by vA!. It runs from November 20 to April 5 next year in the public area on the 1/F to 5/F of vA!, 7A Kennedy Road, Central. Admission is free. For details of the exhibition, please visit its website (www.apo.hk/en/web/apo/va_greenery.html), Facebook page (www.facebook.com/hkvac) or Instagram page (www.instagram.com/hongkongvisualartscentre).

item.title: Five persons arrested during anti-illegal worker operations (with photo)
item.description:
The Immigration Department (ImmD) mounted a series of territory-wide anti-illegal worker operations, including a joint operation with the Hong Kong Police Force (Police) codenamed "Windsand" and a joint operation with Hong Kong Customs (Customs), the Police, the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) and the Leisure and Cultural Services Department (LCSD) in the vicinity of the Kai Tak Sports Park, from November 13 to yesterday (November 19). 
 
     Among the operations mounted, a joint operation was conducted with Customs, the Police, the FEHD and the LCSD during a mega event held from November 13 to 15 and November 17 to combat illegal workers, the sale of infringing goods by mobile hawkers and concert ticket scalping activities, among others, in the vicinity of the Kai Tak Sports Park. During the operation, five suspected illegal workers were arrested by the enforcement officers. The arrested suspected illegal workers were a man and four women, aged 21 to 31. The ImmD and the relevant departments will continue to step up high-profile patrol and enforcement during mega events.
 
     An ImmD spokesman said, "Any person who contravenes a condition of stay in force in respect of him or her shall be guilty of an offence. Also, visitors are not allowed to take employment in Hong Kong, whether paid or unpaid, without the permission of the Director of Immigration. Offenders are liable to prosecution and upon conviction face a maximum fine of $50,000 and up to two years' imprisonment. Aiders and abettors are also liable to prosecution and penalties." 
 
     Under the existing mechanism, the ImmD will, as a standard procedure, conduct an initial screening of vulnerable persons, including illegal workers, illegal immigrants, sex workers and foreign domestic helpers, who are arrested during any operation with a view to ascertaining whether they are trafficking in persons (TIP) and/or forced labour victims. When any TIP and/or forced labour indicator is revealed in the initial screening, the ImmD officers will conduct a full debriefing and identification by using a standardised checklist to ascertain the presence of TIP and/or forced labour elements. Identified TIP and/or forced labour victims will be provided with various forms of support and assistance, including urgent intervention, medical services, counselling, shelter or temporary accommodation and other supporting services. The ImmD calls on TIP and/or forced labour victims to report crimes to the relevant departments immediately.
 
     For reporting illegal employment activities, please call the dedicated hotline 185 185, fax at 2824 1166, email anti_crime@immd.gov.hk, or submit the "Online Reporting of Immigration Offences" form at www.immd.gov.hk.

item.title: Update on mosquito-borne diseases, dengue fever and chikungunya fever
item.description:
The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health today (November 20) announced the latest situation regarding dengue fever (DF) and chikungunya fever (CF). Members of the public are reminded to take appropriate measures to prevent mosquito bites and mosquito breeding, both in Hong Kong and when travelling to areas affected by mosquito-borne diseases, in order to prevent mosquito-borne diseases.

Dengue fever
----------------

     From November 13 to yesterday (November 19), the CHP recorded two imported DF cases. The patients had visited Vietnam and Cambodia respectively during the incubation period.

     Hong Kong has recorded 42 DF cases so far this year, comprising 40 imported cases and two local cases. A total of 59 DF cases were recorded last year (2025), all of which were imported cases. In 2024, 161 DF cases were recorded, comprising 156 imported cases and five local cases.

     According to the World Health Organization (WHO), the global incidence of DF has markedly increased over the past two decades, posing a substantial public health challenge. In 2024, the WHO recorded over 14 million DF cases, which was a record number. In 2025, over 5 million cases and over 4 000 DF-related deaths were reported in over 90 countries/territories. From January to September 2026, around 2.5 million cases and over 1 500 DF-related deaths have been recorded globally.

      DF has long been prevalent in many neighbouring tourist destinations. So far this year, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Sri Lanka and Vietnam each recorded over 100 000 cases; Indonesia recorded over 90 000 cases; Malaysia recorded over 80 000 cases; India recorded over 70 000 cases; and Singapore recorded over 3 000 cases. Meanwhile, according to the Guangdong Provincial Disease Control and Prevention Administration, as of September, Guangdong Province has recorded 586 cases this year, of which 155 were recorded in September.

     Detailed information on the latest DF situation in Hong Kong, as well as neighbouring and overseas countries and areas, has been uploaded to the CHP's website.

Chikungunya fever
-----------------------

     From November 13 to yesterday, the CHP recorded one imported CF case, involving a 71-year-old male. The patient had visited the Chinese Mainland during the incubation period. The CHP considered that the patient was infected during travel and classified the case as imported. He was admitted to hospital for treatment in a mosquito-free environment. He is currently in stable condition. The CHP's epidemiological investigation is ongoing. The case has been reported to the Chinese Mainland health authority.
 
     Hong Kong has recorded nine confirmed CF cases so far this year, including eight imported cases and one local case. Hong Kong recorded a total of 82 confirmed CF cases last year. Among them, 11 were local cases and the rest were imported cases.

    According to the WHO, as of October this year, a total of 363 307 CF cases and 122 CF-related deaths were reported globally. The WHO regions of the Americas and South-East Asia accounted for the largest proportions of reported cases. According to the Guangdong Provincial Disease Control and Prevention Administration, Guangdong Province has recorded 1 753 cases this year (as of September). Among them, 1 014 were recorded in September, a sharp increase compared to the number of cases recorded from July to August (171 to 496 cases).

Preventive measures to be taken by the public
----------------------------------------------------

     The CHP reminds members of the public to maintain good environmental hygiene, and to take appropriate measures to prevent mosquito bites and mosquito breeding, both in Hong Kong and when travelling to areas affected by mosquito-borne diseases, in order to prevent them. Mosquito-borne diseases such as DF and CF are endemic in various countries worldwide. The risk of importation persists. Members of the public should check the situation at their destinations before travelling abroad, especially when travelling to Southeast Asian countries. Additionally, whether travelling or not, members of the public should use DEET-containing insect repellents or other effective active ingredients properly to prevent mosquito bites, but the following precautions should be taken when using them:
 
  • read the label instructions carefully first;
  • apply right before entering an area with a risk of mosquito bites;
  • apply on exposed skin and clothing;
  • use DEET of up to 30 per cent for pregnant women and up to 10 per cent for children (for children who travel to countries or areas where mosquito-borne diseases are endemic or epidemic, and where exposure is likely, those aged 2 months or above can use DEET-containing insect repellents with a DEET concentration of up to 30 per cent);
  • apply sunscreen first, then insect repellent;
  • reapply only when needed and follow the instructions; and
  • in addition to DEET, there are other insect repellents available on the market containing different active ingredients, such as IR3535 and picaridin. When using any insect repellent, the public should follow the usage instructions and precautions on the product label.
     ​
     The Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) appeals to members of the public to continue to stay alert and work together to carry out mosquito prevention and control measures early, including inspecting their homes and surroundings to remove potential breeding grounds, changing water in vases and scrubbing their inner surfaces, removing water in saucers under potted plants at least once a week, and properly disposing of containers such as empty cans and lunch boxes. The FEHD also advises members of the public and property management agencies to keep drains free of blockage and level all defective ground surfaces to prevent the accumulation of water. They should also scrub all drains and surface sewers with an alkaline detergent at least once a week to remove any mosquito eggs.

     ​The public should call 1823 in case of mosquito problems, and may visit the following pages for more information: the CF page of the CHP and the Travel Health Service, the latest Travel Health News, tips for using insect repellents, and the CHP Facebook Page, Instagram Account and YouTube Channel, and also the Mosquito Prevention and Control dedicated page of the FEHD.

item.title: HYAB sets up pavilion for Alliance of Hong Kong Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurial Bases in the Greater Bay Area and holds symposium at Entrepreneur Day 2026 to support young people in pursuing entrepreneurial dreams (with photos)
item.description:
​The Home and Youth Affairs Bureau (HYAB) today (November 20) held a symposium at the Hong Kong Trade Development Council's Entrepreneur Day 2026, and set up a pavilion for the Alliance of Hong Kong Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurial Bases in the Greater Bay Area (the Alliance), showcasing to young entrepreneurs and stakeholders the support of the Alliance and the entrepreneurial opportunities in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA).
      
     The Secretary for Home and Youth Affairs, Miss Alice Mak, said in her opening remarks at the symposium that the Government attaches great importance to youth development. She remarked that the First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (2026-2030) emphasises enhancing youth development opportunities and supporting young people in pursuing their dreams. The Government is committed to encouraging young people to seize the opportunities in the GBA, striving to spark innovation and entrepreneurial spirit among young people and supporting them in pursuing their dreams through the Alliance.
      
     Miss Mak said that the governments of Guangdong and Hong Kong have been providing a wide range of support measures for young people aspiring to start businesses in the GBA, and the entrepreneurial atmosphere in the region has been increasingly vibrant. She expressed gratitude to the Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office of the People's Government of Guangdong Province and the Department of Human Resources and Social Security of Guangdong Province for their staunch support for the work of the Alliance. The HYAB will continue to strengthen co-operation with various stakeholders through the Alliance to support Hong Kong youth in starting businesses in the GBA so that they can actively participate in the development of the GBA and better integrate into and serve the overall development of the country.
      
     Themed "Harnessing the Power of Alliance: Supporting Young People in Pursuing Their Entrepreneurial Dreams", the symposium invited representatives of funded organisations and youth start-up teams under the HYAB Funding Scheme for Youth Entrepreneurship in the GBA, innovation and entrepreneurial bases (I&E bases) in the GBA, and members of the Hong Kong, China youth delegation who attended the official youth innovation and entrepreneurship programme of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) - APEC Young Entrepreneurs Conference earlier, to share how close collaboration between Alliance members and youth start-up teams creates synergy to help Hong Kong youth pursue innovation and entrepreneurship in the GBA. They also shared their insights and takeaways from taking part in the international conference. The HYAB invited representatives of I&E bases from nine Mainland cities of the GBA to introduce local entrepreneurial policies and base services, enabling young entrepreneurs to better grasp the information needed to start and develop their businesses in the GBA and enhance their capabilities and confidence in doing so.
      
     A welcome ceremony for new Alliance members was also held at the symposium to welcome four new member organisations, further expanding the Alliance's network of I&E bases in the GBA.
      
     The Alliance was jointly established by the HYAB, the Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office of the People's Government of Guangdong Province and the Department of Human Resources and Social Security of Guangdong Province in December 2023. It brings together around 70 member organisations from different sectors in Guangdong and Hong Kong, providing young entrepreneurs with a one-stop platform for information, promotion and exchanges. In the nearly three years since its establishment, Alliance members have organised more than 480 activities of various types across Guangdong and Hong Kong, supporting young entrepreneurs at different stages of development and helping them expand their networks and enhance their competitiveness. The I&E bases of the Alliance cover all nine Mainland cities of the GBA.

item.title: HAD opens temporary cold shelters
item.description:
In view of the cold weather, the Home Affairs Department has opened 18 temporary cold shelters in various districts today (November 20) for people in need of the service. The temporary shelters will remain open when the Cold Weather Warning is in force.
      
     Clean mattresses and blankets/quilts, hot meals and hot water will be provided to shelter users free of charge during the opening of the temporary shelters.
           
     To ensure that cold shelter users can rest in a quiet and undisturbed environment, members of the public or agencies wishing to make donations to shelter users are requested to register with the staff of the shelter first. Donors will then be directed to place the donated items at a specified indoor location. The staff will help notify the shelter users to collect the items on their own.

item.title: Woman sentenced to six months' imprisonment for illegally importing alternative smoking products
item.description:
​A woman was sentenced today (November 20) at the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts to six months' imprisonment for illegally importing 38 000 alternative smoking products. The Department of Health (DH) welcomed the verdict and reminded members of the public and visitors not to bring alternative smoking products such as e-cigarettes, heated tobacco products or herbal cigarettes into Hong Kong, and not to use any alternative smoking products.

     The Tobacco and Alcohol Control Office (TACO) of the DH was notified by Hong Kong Customs yesterday (November 19) that 38 000 alternative smoking products had been intercepted in the luggage of the aforesaid woman arriving from Japan. TACO immediately arrested and prosecuted the individual.

     Since the amendments to the Tobacco Control Legislation (Amendment) Ordinance 2025, which conferred arrest powers on TACO inspectors, took effect on September 19, 2025, TACO has prosecuted 34 cases involving the importation of large quantities of alternative smoking products. Thirty-seven persons have been convicted and sentenced to prison terms ranging from four weeks to eight months.

     According to the Import and Export Ordinance (Cap. 60), a person who imports alternative smoking products, including electronic smoking products, heated tobacco products and herbal cigarettes, commits an offence and is liable on summary conviction to a fine of $500,000 and imprisonment for two years; or liable on conviction on indictment to a fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years.

     Under the Smoking (Public Health) Ordinance (Cap. 371), no person may promote, manufacture, sell, or possess for commercial purposes alternative smoking products. An offender is liable to a fine of $50,000 and imprisonment for six months.

     TACO will continue to closely monitor and enforce the law to combat related offences.

     In addition, the DH also cautions the public that alternative smoking products are addictive and are not effective smoking cessation or harm reduction tools. E-cigarettes may increase the risk of cancer, respiratory diseases, and cardiovascular diseases. Smokers are urged to quit smoking as early as possible for their own health and that of others. For assistance, please call the DH's Integrated Smoking Cessation Hotline on 1833 183, or visit www.livetobaccofree.hk for information on quitting.

item.title: Virtual Asset Services Legislation (Amendment) Bill 2026 gazetted
item.description:
The Government published in the Gazette today (November 20) the Virtual Asset Services Legislation (Amendment) Bill 2026. The Bill seeks to expand the regulatory regime for virtual asset (VA) services to cover four additional types of services (including dealing, advisory, management and custody services), with a view to mapping a clear compliance pathway for relevant VA service providers while strengthening protection for investors, thereby fostering the steady and sustainable development of the digital asset market in Hong Kong.

     The Bill proposes to amend the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615), such that any person who carries on a business of providing VA dealing, advisory, management or custody services in Hong Kong will be required to be licensed by or registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), and will be subject to a fit-and-proper test and other relevant regulatory requirements. Banks and stored value facility licensees regulated by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) will also be required to be registered with the SFC if they wish to provide any VA services in Hong Kong. The Bill will equip the SFC and the HKMA with the relevant powers to implement the regime in accordance with the statutory requirements. The proposed regulatory regime under the Bill, while drawing reference from international standards and regulatory trends on anti-money laundering and investor protection in respect of virtual assets, also takes full account of local circumstances and aligns with the standards applicable to conventional financial services in Hong Kong.

     The Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury, Mr Christopher Hui, said, "Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan states that, as guided by the principle of 'same activity, same risks, same regulation', Hong Kong will establish a world-leading regulatory regime for digital assets, thereby improving their liquidity and promoting market innovation. This objective aligns with our vision set out in the Policy Statement 2.0 on the Development of Digital Assets in Hong Kong published last year. This legislative amendment exercise is a key step to materialise our objective and vision above, enhancing the regulatory framework for digital assets in Hong Kong to cover key nodes of relevant market activities, thereby facilitating the establishment of a trusted and sustainable digital asset ecosystem."

     The Chief Executive Officer of the SFC, Ms Julia Leung, said, "The legislative proposal marks an important milestone in completing Hong Kong's regulatory framework for virtual assets. A comprehensive and robust regulatory regime will not only strengthen investor protection, but also provide clear pathways for responsible innovation, laying a solid foundation for the long-term and sustainable development of Hong Kong's digital asset ecosystem."

     The Bill will be introduced into the Legislative Council for First Reading on December 2.

item.title: Test results of seasonal food surveillance project on lap-mei all satisfactory (with photo)
item.description:
The Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department today (November 20) announced the test results of a recently completed seasonal food surveillance project on lap-mei. The test results of all 164 samples collected were satisfactory.

     A spokesman for the CFS said, "Lap-mei is popular in winter and the CFS has therefore collected a variety of lap-mei samples including Chinese pork sausages, Chinese liver sausages, preserved duck meat and preserved pork from different retailers including online retailers for chemical tests and nutrition content analyses."

     Chemical tests targeted veterinary drug residues, metallic contaminants, preservatives usually found in preserved food, as well as other food additives that may be used in the production process and colouring matters that are not permitted in food. For nutrition content analyses, the contents of energy, carbohydrates, protein, total fat, saturated fatty acids, trans fatty acids, sodium and sugars of the samples were tested to check if they were consistent with their declared values on the nutrition label.

     "Members of the public should maintain a balanced diet and avoid excessive consumption of lap-mei in view of its nitrate/nitrite level and potential risk of nitrosamine, as well as the relatively higher sodium, sugar and fat content in some lap-mei. Infants are highly susceptible to nitrite toxicity and should avoid consuming lap-mei, while for young children, the intake of lap-mei should also be restricted.

     "Furthermore, the International Agency for Research on Cancer of the World Health Organization has classified processed meat as 'carcinogenic to humans' (Group 1). The public should avoid excessive consumption of processed meat to reduce the risk of developing colorectal cancer," the spokesman said.

     The spokesman also called on the trade to comply with the legal requirements, follow good manufacturing practices and use permitted food additives in an appropriate manner. Retailers should source food from reliable suppliers and maintain a good recording system in accordance with the Food Safety Ordinance to allow source tracing if needed.

item.title: Two incoming passengers convicted and jailed for importing duty-not-paid cigarettes (with photos)
item.description:
Two incoming passengers were sentenced to five to six months' imprisonment and fined $1,000 to $2,000 by the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts today (November 20) for importing duty-not-paid cigarettes and failing to declare them to Customs officers, in contravention of the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance (DCO) (Cap. 109). One of them was also found to be importing alternative smoking products, in contravention of the Import and Export Ordinance (IEO) (Cap. 60).

     Customs officers intercepted a 47-year-old incoming Mainland female passenger at Hong Kong International Airport (HKIA) on April 14, and seized 26 000 duty-not-paid cigarettes, with an estimated market value of about $106,000 and a duty potential of about $86,000, from her personal baggage. She was immediately arrested, and was sentenced to five months' imprisonment with a fine of $1,000 today.

     Separately, Customs officers intercepted a 58-year-old incoming Mainland male passenger at HKIA yesterday (November 19), and seized about 40 duty-not-paid cigarettes and 40 000 alternative smoking products from his personal baggage. The estimated market value of the seizures is about $120,000 with a duty potential of about $130. He was also immediately arrested, and was sentenced to six months' imprisonment with a fine of $2,000 today.

     Customs welcomes the sentences. The custodial sentences have imposed a considerable deterrent effect and reflect the seriousness of the offences.

     Customs reminds members of the public and travellers that under the DCO, cigarettes are dutiable goods to which the DCO applies. Any person who imports, deals with, possesses, sells or buys illicit cigarettes commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years.

     Under the IEO, any person who imports an alternative smoking product into Hong Kong commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years. 

     Members of the public may report any suspected illicit cigarette activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account (crimereport@customs.gov.hk) or online form (eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002).

item.title: 28 landlords of subdivided units under regulated tenancies convicted of contravening relevant statutory requirements
item.description:
Twenty-eight landlords of subdivided units (SDUs), who contravened Part IVA of the Landlord and Tenant (Consolidation) Ordinance (Cap. 7) (the Ordinance), pleaded guilty and were fined between $800 and $13,600, amounting to a total of $112,500, on November 6, November 13 and today (November 20) at the Eastern Magistrates' Courts. Since the Ordinance came into force, the Rating and Valuation Department (RVD) has continuously strengthened enforcement actions and has prosecuted a total of 1 643 cases to date. Among the 1 478 cases dealt with by the court, all were successfully convicted, which involved a total of 1 291 SDU landlords, amounting to a total of $4,147,040 in fines. In addition, 165 cases are pending a hearing.
      
     The offences of these 28 landlords include (1) failing to submit a Notice of Tenancy (Form AR2) to the Commissioner of Rating and Valuation within 60 days after the term of the regulated tenancy commenced; (2) failing to produce copies of the bills and provide an account in writing when requiring the tenant to pay for the reimbursement of the apportioned water and/or electricity charges; and (3) requesting the tenant to pay money other than the types permitted under the Ordinance (including requiring the tenant to pay an amount of rent for the second-term tenancy exceeding the maximum amount of rent permitted under the Ordinance).

     The RVD earlier discovered that the landlords failed to comply with the relevant requirements under the Ordinance. Upon a comprehensive investigation and evidence collection, the RVD prosecuted the landlords.
 
     A spokesman for the RVD reiterated that SDU landlords must comply with the relevant requirements under the Ordinance, including prohibiting landlords from doing any act calculated to interfere with the peace or comfort of members of the tenant's household, with the intention of causing the tenant to give up occupation of the SDU; or requiring the tenant to pay an amount of rent for the second-term tenancy exceeding the maximum amount of rent permitted under the Ordinance, and also reminded  tenants of their rights under the Ordinance, including a four-year (i.e. two years plus two years) security of tenure. He also stressed that the RVD will continue to take resolute enforcement action against any contraventions of the Ordinance. Apart from following up on reported cases, the RVD has been adopting a multipronged approach to proactively identify, investigate and follow up on cases concerning landlords who are suspected of contravening the Ordinance. In particular, the RVD has been requiring landlords of regulated tenancies to provide information and reference documents of their tenancies for checking whether they have complied with the requirements of the Ordinance. If a landlord, without reasonable excuse, refuses to provide the relevant information or neglects the RVD's request, the landlord commits an offence and is liable to a maximum fine at level 3 ($10,000) and to imprisonment for three months. Depending on the actual circumstances, and having regard to the information and evidence collected, the RVD will take appropriate actions on individual cases, including instigating prosecution against suspected contraventions of the Ordinance.

     To help curb illegal acts as soon as possible, members of the public should report to the RVD promptly any suspected cases of contravening the relevant requirements. Reporting can be made through the telephone hotline (2150 8303), by email (enquiries@rvd.gov.hk), by fax (2116 4920), by post (15/F, Cheung Sha Wan Government Offices, 303 Cheung Sha Wan Road, Kowloon), or in person (visiting the Tenancy Services Section office of the RVD at 7/F, South Tower, Tseung Kwan O Government Offices, 30 Tong Yin Street, Tseung Kwan O, New Territories, and please call 2150 8303 to make an appointment). Furthermore, the RVD has provided a form (Form AR4) (www.rvd.gov.hk/doc/en/forms/ar4.pdf) on its website to enable SDU tenants' reporting to the RVD.
 
     The RVD reminds that pursuant to the Ordinance, a regulated cycle of regulated tenancies is to comprise two consecutive regulated tenancies (i.e. the first-term tenancy and second-term tenancy) for an SDU, and the term of each regulated tenancy is two years. A tenant of a first-term tenancy for an SDU is entitled to be granted a second-term tenancy of the regulated cycle, thus enjoying a total of four years of security of tenure. The RVD has been issuing letters enclosing relevant information to the landlords and tenants concerned of regulated tenancies in batches, according to the expiry time of their first-term tenancies, to assist them in understanding the important matters pertaining to the second-term tenancy, and to remind them about the procedures that need to be followed about two months prior to the commencement of the purported second-term tenancy as well as their respective obligations and rights under the Ordinance. These landlords and tenants may also visit the dedicated page for the second-term tenancy on the RVD's website (www.rvd.gov.hk/en/tenancy_matters/second_term_tenancy.html) for the relevant information, including a concise guide, brochures, tutorial videos and frequently asked questions. The landlords and tenants concerned are also advised to familiarise themselves with the relevant statutory requirements and maintain close communication regarding the second-term tenancy for handling the matters properly and in a timely manner according to the Ordinance.
 
     For enquiries related to regulated tenancies, please call the telephone hotline (2150 8303) or visit the RVD's webpage (www.rvd.gov.hk/en/our_services/part_iva.html) for the relevant information.

item.title: HKICL alerts public of fraudulent website
item.description:
The following is issued on behalf of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority:

     ​Hong Kong Interbank Clearing Limited (HKICL) has recently noted one fraudulent website at fpshk.xyz purported to be from HKICL. If members of the public receive any suspicious communication purportedly from HKICL, please call HKICL's general line at 2533 1111 to verify. Members of the public who suspect that they have become the victim of fraudulent acts should report promptly to the Police.

item.title: Hong Kong Customs detects case involving precious metals and stones dealer carrying out specified cash transaction without Category B registration
item.description:
Hong Kong Customs yesterday (November 19) detected a case involving a local company that conducted a cash transaction of a watch containing precious metals and stones valued at over HK$120,000 while not being a Category B registrant under the Dealers in Precious Metals and Stones Regulatory Regime. The investigation is ongoing.

     According to the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615), unless exempted, any person who is seeking to carry on a business of dealing in precious metals and stones and engage in any transaction(s) (whether making or receiving a payment) with a total value at or above HK$120,000 in Hong Kong is required to register with Hong Kong Customs. 

     In particular, no person other than a Category B registrant may carry out a cash transaction with a total value at or above HK$120,000 in the course of business of dealing in precious metals and stones. Any dealer who is not a Category B registrant, who claims to be a Category B registrant, claims to be authorised to carry out, or carries out any cash transaction(s) with a total value at or above HK$120,000, commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a maximum fine of HK$100,000 and imprisonment for six months.

     Customs reminds dealers in precious metals and stones that they must obtain the relevant registration before they can carry out any cash or non-cash transaction(s) with a total value at or above HK$120,000.

     For the forms, procedures and guidelines to submit applications for registration, please visit the website for Dealers in Precious Metals and Stones Registration System (www.drs.customs.gov.hk) or Customs' webpage (www.customs.gov.hk/en/service-enforcement-information/anti-money-laundering/supervision-of-dealers-in-precious-metals-and-ston/index.html).

     Members of the public may report any suspected transactions involving precious metals and stones with a total value at or above HK$120,000 conducted without the required registration to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account ​(crimereport@customs.gov.hk) or online form (eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002).

item.title: Consumer Price Indices for October 2026
item.description:
The Census and Statistics Department (C&SD) released today (November 20) the Consumer Price Index (CPI) figures for October 2026. According to the Composite CPI, overall consumer prices rose by 2.2% in October 2026 over the same month a year earlier, larger than the corresponding increase (1.9%) in September 2026. The larger increase in October 2026 was mainly due to the end of the rates concession in September 2026. Netting out the effects of all Government's one-off relief measures, the year-on-year rate of increase in the Composite CPI (i.e. the underlying inflation rate) in October 2026 was 2.0%, slightly smaller than that in September 2026 (2.1%).

     On a seasonally adjusted basis, the average monthly rate of increase in the Composite CPI for the 3-month period ending October 2026 was 0.3%, and that for the 3-month period ending September 2026 was 0.2%. Netting out the effects of all Government's one-off relief measures, the corresponding rates of increase were 0.1% and 0.2%.

     Analysed by sub-index, the year-on-year rates of increase in the CPI(A), CPI(B) and CPI(C) were 2.0%, 2.2% and 2.3% respectively in October 2026, as compared to 1.4%, 2.0% and 2.3% respectively in September 2026. Netting out the effects of all Government's one-off relief measures, the year-on-year rates of increase in the CPI(A), CPI(B) and CPI(C) were 1.7%, 2.1% and 2.2% respectively in October 2026, as compared to 1.7%, 2.2% and 2.4% respectively in September 2026.

     On a seasonally adjusted basis, for the 3-month period ending October 2026, the average monthly rates of increase in the CPI(A), CPI(B) and CPI(C) were all 0.3%. The corresponding rates of increase for the 3-month period ending September 2026 were all 0.2%. Netting out the effects of all Government's one-off relief measures, the average monthly rates of increase in the seasonally adjusted CPI(A), CPI(B) and CPI(C) for the 3-month period ending October 2026 were 0.1%, 0.2% and 0.2% respectively, and the corresponding rates of increase for the 3-month period ending September 2026 were all 0.2%.

     Amongst the various components of the Composite CPI, year-on-year increases in prices were recorded in October 2026 for electricity, gas and water (12.7%), miscellaneous services (5.0%), transport (4.5%), durable goods (1.4%), miscellaneous goods (1.4%), housing (1.4%), meals out and takeaway food (0.9%), and clothing and footwear (0.5%).

     On the other hand, year-on-year decreases in the components of the Composite CPI were recorded in October 2026 for basic food (-0.8%), and alcoholic drinks and tobacco (-0.4%).

     Taking the first 10 months of 2026 together, the Composite CPI rose by 1.8% over the same period a year earlier. The respective increases in the CPI(A), CPI(B) and CPI(C) were 1.6%, 1.9% and 1.9% respectively. The corresponding increases after netting out the effects of all Government's one-off relief measures were 1.7%, 1.5%, 1.8% and 1.9% respectively.

     For the 3 months ending October 2026, the Composite CPI rose by 1.9% over the same period a year earlier, while the CPI(A), CPI(B) and CPI(C) rose by 1.6%, 2.0% and 2.2% respectively. The corresponding increases after netting out the effects of all Government's one-off relief measures were 2.0%, 1.7%, 2.1% and 2.2% respectively.

     For the 12 months ending October 2026, the Composite CPI on average rose by 1.7% over the same period a year earlier. The respective increases in the CPI(A), CPI(B) and CPI(C) were 1.5%, 1.8% and 1.8% respectively. The corresponding increases after netting out the effects of all Government's one-off relief measures were 1.6%, 1.4%, 1.7% and 1.8% respectively.

Commentary

     A Government spokesman said that consumer price inflation stayed moderate in October. The underlying Composite CPI rose by 2.0% over a year earlier, slightly lower than the increase of 2.1% in September. Prices of fuel-related items continued to rise noticeably, but spillover effects remained limited, with prices of most other items increasing modestly or declining.

     Looking ahead, earlier increases in international oil prices will continue to feed through to local consumer prices of fuel-related items. However, price pressures on other fronts should remain broadly in check, keeping overall inflation moderate. Nevertheless, geopolitical tensions remain a key source of near-term uncertainty for international fuel prices and warrant close monitoring.

Further information

     The CPIs and year-on-year rates of change at section level for October 2026 are shown in Table 1.
