item.title: Speech by CE at APEC Next-Gen Young Entrepreneurs Summit 2026 (English only) (with video)
item.description:
Following is the video speech by the Chief Executive, Mr John Lee, at the APEC Next-Gen Young Entrepreneurs Summit 2026 today (November 20):

Executive Director Eduardo Pedrosa (Executive Director of the APEC Secretariat); Director Antonio I. Basilio (Director of the APEC Business Advisory Council International Secretariat); Chairman Jaime Sze (Founding and Honourable Life Chairman of The Y.Elites Association and Chairman of The Y.Elites Foundation); Chairman Jason Wong (Chairman of The Y.Elites Association); President Lyu Xiaoning (President and Co-Founder of the Asia Pacific Young Entrepreneurs Alliance); distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen,

     Good morning. I am delighted to welcome you to Hong Kong, Asia's world city, and to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Next-Gen Young Entrepreneurs Summit, the fourth edition.

     You are young entrepreneurs, emerging and established business leaders, investors and professionals. You come from finance and technology, manufacturing, green industries, healthcare, the creative economy and much more. And you're here to build cross-economy connections, contribute to APEC policy considerations and, ultimately, advance market-driven growth throughout the APEC region.

     The Summit's theme, "From Ideas to Impact: Young Entrepreneurs Driving Asia-Pacific Growth", speaks to APEC's future - and yours. We live in an era of accelerating change, where technologies such as AI are reshaping economies, businesses and everyday life. New tools are breaking down old barriers to innovation, transcending borders and connecting talent across APEC economies. And they're doing so faster than ever before. Yet technology alone is not enough to turn promising ideas into society-wide solutions.

     What drives progress is the creativity and collaborative spirit of young entrepreneurs like yourselves - people who dare to reimagine industries, solve community challenges, and build enterprises rooted in shared prosperity.

     Under Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan, our strategic blueprint for Hong Kong's economic and social development, Hong Kong will expand opportunities for youth development. It will help nurture a new generation with a deep affection for our country, China, and for Hong Kong, while holding a global perspective and an ambitious, positive mindset. The Plan will encourage young people to seize opportunities in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. It will spark their innovative and entrepreneurial spirit and support them in pursuing their dreams.

     Soon after assuming office, this term of Government produced Hong Kong's first Youth Development Blueprint. Over the past four years, we have launched more than 340 measures under the Blueprint to promote youth development and create concrete opportunities for young people.

     We share a common vision with APEC economies - empowering future generations. To that end, we promote exchanges among young entrepreneurs and professionals, as well as internships and other learning experiences. This Summit, an international gathering committed to helping young entrepreneurs gain invaluable experience and unlock fresh opportunities, smartly reflects our youth goals.

     APEC has long promoted open dialogue, inclusive trade and practical co-operation across its diverse economies. For young innovators, it opens doors to new markets, to mentorship from industry leaders, to cross-border partnerships, and to policy support that turns vision into reality.

     And Hong Kong, the international hub at the heart of the Greater Bay Area, is your launching pad. We connect the Chinese Mainland and the world at large, offering professional services, ready access to capital, and a thriving environment for start-ups to test, grow and expand across the wide-ranging APEC region.

     Ladies and gentlemen, I wish you an inspiring Summit and an unforgettable stay in Hong Kong, the world's rising East-meets-West centre for international cultural exchange. Thank you.

item.title: Speech by CE at InfraEX Week 2026 Grand Opening Ceremony (English only) (with photos/video)
item.description:
Following is the speech by the Chief Executive, Mr John Lee, at the InfraEX Week 2026 Grand Opening Ceremony today (November 20):

Honourable Vice Minister Liu Dongshun (Vice Minister of Water Resources of the People's Republic of China), distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen,

     Good morning. I am pleased to welcome you to Hong Kong and the Grand Opening Ceremony of the inaugural InfraEX Week, which brings together some 800 infrastructure project leaders, government officials and high-profile professionals from over 30 countries and economies, with an additional 1 000 expected to join online.

     We are here to take in three concurrent signature events: the second International Infrastructure and Projects Leaders Summit, the International Conference on Modular Construction, and the Construction Innovation Expo – all now under the brand umbrella of InfraEX Week.

     The theme of this year's summit is "Envisioning a Sustainable Future: From Insights to Impacts". In a world shaped by shifting geopolitics, urgent climate challenges and rapid technological advance, insights alone are not enough. We must turn ideas into projects with lasting impact – through innovation, collaboration and, more importantly, clear strategic direction.

     Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan offers exactly that. Closely aligned with the National 15th Five-Year Plan, it provides a strategic roadmap for Hong Kong's future, while enabling Hong Kong to better integrate into, and serve, the overall national development of our country, China.

     Our plan builds on real strengths. Hong Kong ranks number one in the world in economic freedom, second globally in competitiveness and third as a financial centre, while remaining among the international leaders in initial public offerings.

     More than rankings, these and other recognitions reflect the world's confidence in Hong Kong, its sterling capabilities and promising future. Our Five-Year Plan builds on this confidence, giving businesses, investors and innovators strategic insight into the city's development and emerging opportunities.

     A clear example is the Northern Metropolis. Central to the Five-Year Plan, and expressly supported by the National 15th Five-Year Plan, the Northern Metropolis takes up one-third of Hong Kong's geographical area. It will eventually be home to some 2.5 million people – one-third of Hong Kong's population. It is expected to create 500 000 new job opportunities and account for some 13 per cent of Hong Kong's GDP.

     The Hong Kong Park of the Hetao Shenzhen-Hong Kong Science and Technology Innovation Co-operation Zone, located within the Northern Metropolis, is being developed as a world-class I&T hub. It will enable cross-boundary flows of personnel, materials, capital, data and other elements driving innovation.

     And the Northern Metropolis' San Tin Technopole, Hung Shui Kiu Industry Park and Advanced Construction Industry Park will support the growth of wide-ranging industries, including a more innovative, productive and sustainable construction sector.

     We are also pressing ahead with the development of three Northern Metropolis university towns in San Tin, Hung Shui Kiu and Ta Kwu Ling. Each will integrate innovation, industry and education with community life, creating vibrant centres where people can enjoy living, working, learning and thriving.

     The university towns will build on Hong Kong's globally recognised strengths in higher education. In the latest QS Asia University Rankings, five Hong Kong universities ranked in Asia's top 10, including three in the top five. Globally, let me add, five of our universities rank in the world's top 100.

     To build the Northern Metropolis and all that it promises, we must deliver infrastructure that is truly future-ready. And that means quality more than quantity. Our Five-Year Plan reinforces this with its smart city concept embedded in the planning of transport, housing, green spaces and other public facilities.

     Artificial intelligence is a key enabler of this vision. And we are accelerating its adoption across industries, particularly construction, to optimise resource allocation, enhance project productivity, and improve cost-effectiveness.

     Building smarter goes beyond AI. We are also embracing advanced engineering technologies and innovative construction methods and materials. These change how infrastructure is delivered. By promoting high-productivity methods, deploying construction robots and expanding the use of digital works supervision systems, we are turning innovation into practical, on-the-ground improvements.

     Our impact extends beyond our boundaries. The National 15th Five-Year Plan calls for enhancing the construction sector's global standing and competitiveness, and Hong Kong is well placed to contribute. We connect our country's capabilities with international opportunities and provide professional support to turn them into successful projects.

     Our strength lies in our services expertise as well. From engineering and project management to legal and financial services, Hong Kong professionals combine cross-boundary experience with expertise in international standards and practices. We help Mainland construction enterprises in their business expansion, while supporting international partners seeking opportunities in the Greater Bay Area, the markets of the Belt and Road and beyond.

     We also help showcase our country's advanced construction technologies and materials through research, testing, certification and application. A notable example is the world's first pedestrian footbridge built with S960 high-strength steel produced in our country.

     The project brought together Hong Kong's academic research expertise and public works experience, showing how advanced materials can be applied under Hong Kong's internationally aligned regulatory framework.

     This demonstrates Hong Kong's role as a "super connector" and "super value-adder": bridging standards and validating innovation. It sets a reference for interoperability between Chinese and international standards, paving the way for wider adoption of our country's construction standards worldwide.

     Ladies and gentlemen, excellence in the construction industry depends on a great many factors, none more important than collaboration. Today's summit brings together policymakers, financiers, planners, engineers, builders and technology providers, here to gain intelligence and insight, create partnerships, and develop projects with lasting impact.

     Collaboration will take concrete shape shortly, I am pleased to say, as we will witness the exchange of MOUs and a Letter of Intent with our international and local partners.

     I wish you the best of infrastructure business at the inaugural InfraEX Week, and a memorable stay in Hong Kong, Asia's World City. Thank you.

item.title: HKETO, Washington DC promotes new opportunities for global business (with photos)
item.description:
The Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in Washington, DC (HKETO, Washington DC) on November 19 (Washington time) briefed the US-China Business Council (USCBC) at a "lunch and learn" event entitled "Hong Kong's New Opportunities for Global Business" on new business opportunities in Hong Kong across various sectors further to the announcement of the 2026 Policy Address and the First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (2026-2030) (First Five-Year Plan). Attendees included members of the USCBC, who are multinational US-based companies with a presence and/or interest in the Greater China region. 

     The Director of the HKETO, Washington DC, Ms Elania Luk, began her remarks by emphasising Hong Kong's critical role in facilitating global connections. "We are a 'super connector'", Ms Luk said. "Hong Kong has always been about connecting people, businesses, and markets. We provide international companies with a strategic platform to access the Chinese Mainland and the wider Asia-Pacific region."
      
     Ms Luk outlined Hong Kong's economic development priorities under the 2026 Policy Address and the First Five-Year Plan, emphasising the city's commitment to long-term growth, international engagement, and closer business co-operation.

     She highlighted Hong Kong's established strengths in financial services, trade, maritime and aviation, alongside its growing focus on innovation and technology. Hong Kong's role as "Four Centres, One Hub" reinforces the city's international competitiveness while creating new avenues for investment and commercial collaboration. She also highlighted opportunities in Hong Kong's legal and dispute resolution services, including the city's plans to become a capital for mediation and arbitration.

     Ms Luk provided an update on the Northern Metropolis, Hong Kong's largest development project in history. Covering approximately one-third of the city's land area, the development is designed to integrate education, technology, research, and talent, while taking advantage of its proximity to the Greater Bay Area's extensive supply chains and innovation ecosystem.

     "The Northern Metropolis presents an exciting opportunity for American companies," Ms Luk said. "American businesses have world-class expertise in many of the sectors that will be important to this project. We welcome their participation and look forward to exploring opportunities for greater co-operation."

     Ms Luk remarked that at a time when businesses are navigating an increasingly complex global environment, Hong Kong remains open. "Our message to American companies is simple: Hong Kong is a place to connect, invest and grow. We have always welcomed American businesses to be part of our growth."

     Following her remarks, the Head of Business and Talent Attraction/Investment Promotion of Invest Hong Kong New York Office, Ms Yi Xie, spoke about how these developments create opportunities for the business community. She explained how Invest Hong Kong can provide bespoke services to US companies wishing to set up or expand operations in Hong Kong.

item.title: "Sighting Dragons in the Field: An Exhibition of Dinosaur Fossils from Port Island and the Chinese Mainland" opens (with photos)
item.description:
The opening ceremony of "Sighting Dragons in the Field: An Exhibition of Dinosaur Fossils from Port Island and the Chinese Mainland" was held today (November 19) at the Hong Kong Heritage Discovery Centre. Jointly presented by the Development Bureau (DEVB) and the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology (IVPP) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, the exhibition features dinosaur fossils discovered on Port Island, unveiling the mystery of Hong Kong's giant dinosaur. It also offers a comprehensive overview of the evolution and paleoecological landscape of dinosaurs in China by showcasing fossil treasures from other parts of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) and various parts of the country.

     Speaking at the opening ceremony, the Secretary for Development, Ms Bernadette Linn, said that excavation work for the dinosaur fossils on Port Island commenced in October 2024. With preparation and research work gradually completed, the exhibition not only marks the rare discovery of dinosaur fossils in Hong Kong for the first time, but also highlights the fossils' reflection of the prominence of the dinosaurs in their era, the history they preserved, and Hong Kong's palaeoenvironment. She expressed special gratitude to the IVPP for providing professional guidance and assistance in the excavation, preparation and research of the dinosaur fossils, as well as in exhibit selection, curation and the loan of precious fossil specimens for display. She also thanked the Natural History Museum of Guangxi, the Zhejiang Museum of Natural History and the Zhucheng Dinosaur Culture Research Center in Shandong for co-organising the exhibition and lending valuable collections. Through the curatorial team's careful planning, the exhibition brings together dinosaur fossils from different places for joint display and dialogue, telling good stories of dinosaurs.

     The Director of the IVPP, Professor Xu Xing, said in the ceremony that the collaboration marks an important milestone in Hong Kong's palaeontological research. He expressed gratitude to the DEVB for its full support of the collaborative research and popular science education initiatives. Professor Xu hoped that through the exhibition, members of the public can learn about the latest research findings on the Port Island dinosaur fossils, recognise Hong Kong's unique position in the evolutionary history of dinosaurs in China and worldwide, and gain opportunities to closely engage with palaeontology to enhance their interest in and knowledge of prehistoric life.

     Other officiating guests at the opening ceremony were the Permanent Secretary for Development (Works), Mr Ricky Lau; the Chairman of the Antiquities Advisory Board, Professor Desmond Hui; and the Chairman of the Advisory Committee on Built Heritage Conservation, Professor Douglas So.

     The exhibition features 66 sets of invaluable exhibits, including all the dinosaur fossils unearthed on Port Island, as well as Cretaceous dinosaur fossils from other parts of the GBA and areas of the Mainland beyond Guangdong Province. Of the 46 sets of fossils from the Mainland, 34 are National Class I key protection fossils. Most of the fossils from the Mainland are on display in Hong Kong for the first time. Highlights of the exhibition include the dinosaur fossils unearthed from Port Island (several bones of which are likely from a single titanosauriform dinosaur); the Asiatyrannus xui skeleton with a complete cranium; the Banji long cranium fossil featuring a prominent bony crest and no teeth in either the upper or lower jaws; the gigantic Zhuchengtyrannus magnus jawbone fossils; elongated eggs laid by oviraptorosaurs; and dinosaur egg fossils preserved with embryos.

     Supplemented by models, the exhibition illustrates the evolution of dinosaurs in China in an easy-to-understand manner. To promote palaeontology-related knowledge, the Hong Kong Heritage Discovery Centre will organise a series of public talks and diverse workshops, offering the public an in-depth understanding of palaeontological fossils and palaeoecology.

     Admission to the exhibition is free. Details are as follows:

Date: November 20, 2026, to May 12, 2027
Opening hours: 
Monday to Wednesday and Friday: 10am to 6pm
Saturday, Sunday and public holidays: 10am to 7pm
Closed on Thursdays (except public holidays), the first and second days of Chinese New Year
Venue: Hong Kong Heritage Discovery Centre, Kowloon Park, Haiphong Road, Tsim Sha Tsui

     For details of the exhibition, related activities, and highlight videos, please visit the Antiquities and Monuments Office's website (www.amo.gov.hk/en/visitor-centre/exhibitions/heritage-discovery-centre/dinosaur-exhibition/index.html).

item.title: Hong Kong ICT Awards 2026 celebrates 20th anniversary and recognises outstanding ICT achievements (with photos)

Having won the Smart Business Grand Award for "AI-enabled Smart Water Tank Cleaning Robot", Electrical and Mechanical Services Department/Architectural Services Department/Housing Department/Hong Kong Center for Construction Robotics Limited/Hong Kong Housing Society also claimed the highest honour of this year's competition.

     Addressing the presentation ceremony, Mr Chan said, "Look back at the winners over the years, and you can see how much has changed. The technology has changed. But the winners have something in common: they saw what people needed and found a new way to help."
      
     Mr Chan noted that some of the most important applications of artificial intelligence (AI) may still lie ahead. "AI can help us do familiar things better. The more interesting question is: what may it allow us to do differently? Many of the winners tonight are pointing the way. They show us not just what AI can do, but what it makes possible for people," he said.
      
     He added that the Government's role is to give innovators the conditions to succeed. item.title: Excessive cadmium found in imported crab sample
item.description:
The Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department today (November 19) announced that an imported crab sample from the Philippines was detected to contain cadmium, a metallic contaminant, at a level exceeding the legal limit. The CFS is following up on the incident. 
 
     "The CFS collected the above-mentioned crab sample at the import level for testing under its routine Food Surveillance Programme. The test result showed that the sample contained cadmium at a level of 5.6 parts per million (ppm), exceeding the legal limit of 2 ppm. The affected batch of the product has not entered the market," a spokesman for the CFS said. 

     "Long-term excessive intake of cadmium may affect kidney functions. The CFS has informed the importer concerned of the irregularity. Should there be sufficient evidence, prosecution will be instituted," the spokesman added. 

     According to the Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations (Cap. 132V), any person who sells food with metallic contamination above the legal limit is liable upon conviction to a maximum fine of $50,000 and imprisonment for six months. 

     The CFS will alert the Philippine authorities and the trade, and will continue to follow up on the incident and take appropriate action. An investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Speech by FS at presentation ceremony for Hong Kong ICT Awards 2026 (English only) (with photos/video)
item.description:
Following is the speech by the Financial Secretary, Mr Paul Chan, at the presentation ceremony for the Hong Kong ICT Awards 2026 today (November 19):

Professor Alexander Wai (Chairman of the Grand Judging Panel of the Hong Kong ICT Awards 2026 and the President and Vice-Chancellor of Hong Kong Baptist University), Professor Sun Dong (Secretary for Innovation, Technology and Industry), distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen, 

     Good evening. It is a great pleasure to join you tonight to celebrate the 20th anniversary of the Hong Kong ICT Awards, and to honour the winners this year.

     Twenty years ago this month, the very first awards were presented right here in this venue. The Award of the Year went to a Wi-Fi base station. The iPhone had yet to be unveiled.

     Look back at the winners over the years, and you can see how much has changed. An app that lets you catch virtual butterflies on a smartphone. A ring that screens for sleep apnoea at home. Biometric technology that helps travellers move more quickly through our airport. And last year, an AI system that spots defects on the production line.

     The technology has changed. But the winners have something in common: they saw what people needed and found a new way to help.

     This year's theme is "Innovate, Inspire, Impact". Sometimes an inventor sees a need and creates something new. Sometimes it works the other way round, where an invention inspires someone else to take it in a new direction. 

     The story of the laser is a case in point. In 1960, the first laser was switched on in California. It was a remarkable achievement, but few at the time could have foreseen its impact. Indeed, the laser was once described as "a solution looking for a problem".

     Today, lasers are at work everywhere from the operating theatre to the supermarket checkout. But one of the most far-reaching applications came from Professor Charles Kao and his colleague George Hockham. Sixty years ago, they proposed that, if the glass were pure enough, light could carry information over long distances through a glass fibre. That insight helped lay the foundations for the Internet. In 2009, Professor Kao shared the Nobel Prize in Physics.

     I believe we are at a similar moment with AI. AI has already found many use cases. But, as with the laser, some of its most important applications may still lie ahead. AI can help us do familiar things better. The more interesting question is: what may it allow us to do differently? We may reinvent a business model, redesign a service or rethink how we teach and learn. Many of the winners tonight are pointing the way. They show us not just what AI can do, but what it makes possible for people.

     For the Government, our role is to give innovators like you the conditions to succeed. Through the Committee on AI+ and Industry Development Strategy, we are helping more industries put AI to work. That takes computing power. The data facility cluster now under construction at Sandy Ridge will expand Hong Kong's computing capacity. It also takes research. The Hong Kong AI Research and Development Institute will help turn research breakthroughs into practical applications. And it takes people, too. We are training specialists to lead this work, while our "AI for All" programme helps people across the community use AI with confidence. 

     Ladies and gentlemen, over the past 20 years, these Awards have brought together a community of innovators. The Winner Circle, launched this year, brings together people who have won in different years and across different categories. It gives them the chance to learn from one another and pass on what they have learned to the newcomers and next generations. 

     To the students and young innovators with us tonight, let me return to the phone in your pocket. It looks very different from the phones we used 20 years ago. Twenty years from now, the tools in your hands will have changed even more. But the future will still belong to those who use technology well and dare to push the boundaries of what it can do.

     Let me thank the organisers, the eight industry bodies leading the award categories, and Professor Wai and the Grand Judging Panel. Your dedication and rigour give these Awards their standing.

     To all our winners, my warmest congratulations again. Six decades ago, Professor Charles Kao showed us how far a single technology could travel. I hope the ideas and applications we celebrate tonight will make a difference here in Hong Kong and well beyond. 

     Thank you, and have a wonderful evening.

item.title: International Young Talent Exchange Base officially launches (with photos)
item.description:
​The Home and Youth Affairs Bureau (HYAB) today (November 19) held the inaugural event of the International Youth Talent Exchange Base (the Base) at HYAB JC Y Cube, marking the Base's official establishment with an aim of further fostering youth development and international exchange.
      
     The Chief Executive announced the establishment of the Base in the 2026 Policy Address to promote international exchanges by inviting global experts and visiting guests to engage with young people who have participated in overseas exchange and internship programmes. Themed "Youth Connecting to the World: Unlocking Global Opportunities with WIPO's Leaders", today's inaugural event invited a delegation led by the Deputy Director General of the World Intellectual Property Organisation (WIPO), Dr Shen Changyu, to exchange with Hong Kong young people, including Youth Link members who have taken part in the HYAB's youth entrepreneurship, internship and international exchange programmes, enabling them to learn about the latest developments in the global intellectual property economy and the opportunities available to young people.
      
     In her speech at the inaugural event, the Secretary for Home and Youth Affairs, Miss Alice Mak, said that under the First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (2026–2030), the Government is committed to enhancing youth development opportunities, and supporting young people in pursuing their dreams. To realise this vision, the Chief Executive announced in the 2026 Policy Address that the HYAB would establish the Base this year to further promote youth development. Through the Base, the HYAB will open up more opportunities for young people to go global and host dynamic activities at the Base to broaden their international horizons, while inviting members of Youth Link to actively participate, with a view to gathering global youth talent and fostering cross-cultural exchanges.
      
     Before the WIPO delegation's sharing session, Miss Mak hosted a plaque-unveiling ceremony for the Base with other officiating guests, including Dr Shen; the Permanent Secretary for Home and Youth Affairs, Mr Patrick Li; the Deputy Director-General of the Education and Youth Department of the Liaison Office of the Central People's Government in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Ms Wan Ning; the Director-General of the International Department of the Office of the Commissioner of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Mr Wong Jian; the Under Secretary for Home and Youth Affairs, Mr Clarence Leung; the Commissioner for Youth, Mr Andy Lam, and representatives of the management and operating organisations of the Base.
      
     The Base covers three youth facilities, namely the "HYAB JC Y Cube at Youth Square in Chai Wan, "Youth Link · Nam Cheong" at the Nam Cheong District Community Centre in Sham Shui Po, and the Youth Post, "Runway 1331" in Kai Tak.

item.title: CE attends APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen (with photos/videos)
item.description:
The Chief Executive, Mr John Lee, today (November 19) attended the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, exchanging views with leaders of other economies on deepening regional co-operation and expanding into diversified markets.
 
     Speaking at the meeting, Mr Lee said that the Asia-Pacific region is today's economic growth engine, providing two-thirds of global growth. As an international finance, trade and innovation centre, and benefitting from the national support, the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region will give full play to its significant role as a "super connector" and "super value-adder". Hong Kong will continue to maintain a free and open market, embrace the rules-based multilateral trading system, and look forward to expanding its co-operation with APEC, to continuously contribute to the region and work hand in hand towards shared prosperity.
 
     Mr Lee said that the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area is an important platform for open co-operation and high-quality development. The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting is taking place in Shenzhen, and the APEC Finance Ministers' Meeting was held in Hong Kong for the first time last month, demonstrating the Greater Bay Area's international relevance and competitiveness. In the top 100 innovation clusters of the Global Innovation Index 2026, the Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Guangzhou cluster ranks first globally for two consecutive years, demonstrating the fruitful results of mutually beneficial co-operation among sister cities in the Greater Bay Area in the field of innovation and technology. Innovation is central to future competitiveness. Hong Kong's world-class universities and research institutions, together with the manufacturing and commercial strength of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, jointly promote the transformation and applications of research and development outcomes. Hong Kong is actively promoting the broad-based application of artificial intelligence to promote high-quality development.
 
     APEC member economies reached a consensus on the Leaders' Declaration, and adopted leader-level outcome documents on trade digitalisation, digital economy, emerging technologies, and connectivity. Mr Lee said these forward-looking outcomes play a crucial role in advancing practical co-operation in the Asia-Pacific region, deepening regional economic integration and promoting high-quality development.
 
     In the afternoon, Mr Lee met and held bilateral meetings with leaders of other economies. During his meeting with the President of Peru, Ms Keiko Fujimori, Mr Lee said that Peru is Hong Kong's sixth-largest trading partner in Latin America, and he was pleased to have personally witnessed the signing of a Free Trade Agreement between Hong Kong and Peru in Lima, Peru, in 2024, covering areas such as trade in goods, trade in services and investment. The Agreement officially entered into force on September 1 this year, further promoting bilateral trade and investment and marking a new milestone in economic and trade relations between the two places. He encouraged more Peruvian enterprises to make good use of Hong Kong's international trading platform and professional services, and to use Hong Kong as a springboard to enter the Mainland and Asian markets and explore more business opportunities. Hong Kong will continue to expand into emerging markets, give full play to its roles as a "super connector" and "super value-adder", and pursue more co-operation with Peru in different areas for mutual benefit and win-win outcomes.
　　
     Mr Lee afterwards met with the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance of Singapore, Mr Lawrence Wong. Mr Lee said he was pleased to meet Mr Wong again in Shenzhen following their meeting in Hong Kong in March this year. Mr Lee said that both Hong Kong and Singapore are highly externally oriented international financial and trade centres. The two places enjoy frequent economic, trade and people-to-people exchanges and maintain close co-operation. The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government is accelerating the development of the Northern Metropolis and the Hong Kong Park of the Hetao Shenzhen-Hong Kong Science and Technology Innovation Co-operation Zone. Mr Lee encouraged Singaporean enterprises with strengths in innovation and technology to establish a presence in the Northern Metropolis and tap into the Mainland market by leveraging Hong Kong's advantages in bringing together global talent and frontier research. He was also thankful to Singapore for its continued support for Hong Kong's early accession to the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership, and expressed the hope that, with Singapore assuming the Association of Southeast Asian Nations chairmanship next year, the two sides would continue to deepen collaboration and jointly promote regional economic development.
 
     Mr Lee concluded the meetings and related events in Shenzhen and returned to Hong Kong in the evening.

item.title: Hong Kong Customs conducts interdepartmental anti-illicit cigarette publicity campaign at Choi Ying Estate (with photos)
item.description:
Hong Kong Customs today (November 19) conducted a joint anti-illicit cigarette publicity campaign with a member of the Kwun Tong District Council, the Tobacco and Alcohol Control Office (TACO) of the Department of Health, the Housing Department (HD) and the Hong Kong Police Force at Choi Ying Estate. Customs also publicised the Duty Stamp System. 

     Customs officers patrolled the housing estate and introduced to residents Customs' enforcement actions against illicit cigarettes, and reminded them that the maximum penalty for offences related to duty-not-paid cigarettes has been increased to a $2 million fine and seven years' imprisonment. Customs also explained to estate security personnel how to deal with suspected illicit cigarette activities.

     Customs officers also introduced the Duty Stamp System, which is to be implemented in Hong Kong, to the District Council member and residents. The three-month Pilot Run for the Duty Stamp System launched by Customs concluded early this year. The department will continue to maintain close communication with all stakeholders and optimise the design and implementation details of the system. Customs expects the Duty Stamp System to achieve the ultimate goal of effective differentiation of duty-paid cigarettes from duty-not-paid ones, and to combat "cheap whites".

     Customs will continue to strengthen publicity and education to raise public awareness of anti-illicit cigarettes. If public rental housing units are found to be involved in illicit cigarette crimes, Customs will notify the HD for follow-up action after the conclusion of court proceedings. Customs reminds members of the public not to buy or sell illicit cigarettes or distribute illicit cigarette leaflets to avoid creating a criminal record that could affect their future. 

     Under the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance (Cap. 109), anyone involved in dealing with, possession of, selling or buying illicit cigarettes commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years. Members of the public are urged to report any suspected illicit cigarette activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080, its dedicated crime-reporting email account (crimereport@customs.gov.hk) or online form (eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002). 

     In accordance with the Smoking (Public Health) Ordinance (Cap. 371), no person shall distribute any smoking product advertisement (including any promotional leaflet). Any person who contravenes the regulation is liable to a maximum fine of $50,000. Members of the public are also urged to report any suspected activities of illicit cigarette leaflet distribution to TACO's hotline 2961 8823.

item.title: Incoming passenger convicted and jailed for importing duty-not-paid cigarettes (with photo)
item.description:
An incoming male passenger was sentenced to seven months' imprisonment and fined $2,000 by the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts today (November 19) for importing duty-not-paid cigarettes and failing to declare them to Customs officers, in contravention of the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance (DCO).

     Customs officers intercepted a 55-year-old Mainland male passenger arriving in Hong Kong from Tokyo, Japan, at Hong Kong International Airport yesterday (November 18) and seized about 41 800 duty-not-paid cigarettes, with an estimated market value of about $209,000 and a duty potential of about $138,100, from his personal baggage. The passenger was subsequently arrested.

     Customs welcomes the sentence. The custodial sentence has imposed a considerable deterrent effect and reflects the seriousness of the offences. 

     Customs reminds members of the public that under the DCO, cigarettes are dutiable goods to which the DCO applies. Any person who deals with, possesses, sells or buys illicit cigarettes commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years.

     Members of the public may report any suspected illicit cigarette activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account (crimereport@customs.gov.hk) or online form (eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002).

item.title: HKICL alerts public of fraudulent website
item.description:
The following is issued on behalf of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority:

     Hong Kong Interbank Clearing Limited (HKICL) has recently noted a fraudulent website at fpstk.xyz purported to be from HKICL. The fraudulent website imitates as "Buyer Online Protection" to provide services including 1) refund to buyer, 2) unauthorised online transaction reporting, and 3) online transaction support, for online transaction over FPS payment.      HKICL urges the public to beware of suspicious calls, websites or other communications, and to remain vigilant in protecting personal information. Members of the public who suspect that they have become the victim of fraudulent acts should report promptly to the Police.

item.title: DH's Medical Device Advisory Panel holds inaugural meeting (with photos)
item.description:
​The Medical Device Advisory Panel (the Advisory Panel) under the Department of Health (DH) held its inaugural meeting today (November 19) to provide advice on a new statutory regulatory regime for medical devices that the Government is actively preparing to establish. The aim is to enhance the regulation of medical devices supplied in Hong Kong with respect to safety, quality and performance, thereby safeguarding public health, promoting orderly and sustainable development of the medical device industry, and developing Hong Kong into an international health and medical innovation hub.
      
     The Advisory Panel is chaired by Professor Philip Chiu. Panel members are representatives from the medical, engineering, and innovation and technology sectors. A complete list of members is available on the website of the DH's Medical Device Division.
      
     The First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (2026-2030) and The Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address state that the Government will comprehensively intensify the regulatory reform of drugs and medical devices, enhance the regulatory regime, and establish the Centre for Medical Products Regulation. The Government is systematically advancing a number of initiatives, including taking forward legislative reform to establish a new statutory regulatory regime for medical devices that covers all aspects of risk management stages before and after medical devices are placed on the market. The DH aims to broadly and comprehensively gather valuable insights from various stakeholders through the Advisory Panel to establish a statutory regulatory framework for medical devices that is clear, practicable, forward-looking, tailored to Hong Kong's circumstances and aligned with international standards, thereby providing stronger institutional support for Hong Kong's development as an international health and medical innovation hub.
      
     At the meeting, DH representatives presented the achievements of the current Medical Device Administrative Control System (MDACS), which has been operating for over 20 years on a voluntary basis, as well as the Government's legislative proposal on regulating medical devices in Hong Kong. The Advisory Panel fully supports the Government in advancing the relevant legislative work in accordance with the following key principles:
 
  1. to safeguard public safety and health;  
  2. to promote innovation;
  3. to align with international regulatory standards;
  4. to build on the experience of the local administrative system;
  5. to focus on control at source and require upstream traders in the supply chain to obtain licences; and
  6. to implement tiered registration of medical devices in an orderly manner in accordance with the risk-based principle.
 
     In addition to gathering and conveying stakeholders' feedback to the DH during the establishment of the statutory regulatory regime for medical devices, the Advisory Panel will also advise the DH on the operation and transitional arrangements of the MDACS.

item.title: Kazakhstan's ADILI debuts first international store in Hong Kong, spotlighting growing Central Asian ties (with photos)

item.title: Import of poultry meat and products from areas in Norway, UK and Netherlands suspended
item.description:
The Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department announced today (November 19) that in view of notifications from the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) about outbreaks of highly pathogenic H5N1 avian influenza in the Lindesnes Municipality of Agder County in Norway, the West Lindsey District of Lincolnshire County in the United Kingdom (UK), and the Province of Friesland in the Netherlands, the CFS has instructed the trade to suspend the import of poultry meat and products (including poultry eggs) from the above-mentioned areas with immediate effect to protect public health in Hong Kong. 

     A CFS spokesman said that Hong Kong has currently established a protocol with Norway for the import of poultry meat but not for poultry eggs. According to the Census and Statistics Department, Hong Kong imported about 20 tonnes of frozen poultry meat from Norway, about 680 tonnes of chilled and frozen poultry meat and about 220 000 poultry eggs from the UK, and about 790 tonnes of frozen poultry meat from the Netherlands in the first nine months of this year. 

     "The CFS has contacted the Norwegian, British and Dutch authorities over the issues and will closely monitor information issued by the WOAH and the relevant authorities on the avian influenza outbreaks. Appropriate action will be taken in response to the development of the situation," the spokesman said.

item.title: Hong Kong Intellectual Property Academy launched to nurture cross-disciplinary talent and promote commercialisation of innovation outcomes (with photos)
item.description:
The Hong Kong Intellectual Property (IP) Academy was officially launched today (November 19) to provide more systematic and recognised on-the-job IP training for practitioners across different sectors, expand Hong Kong's IP talent pool, and support Hong Kong in deepening its development as a regional IP trading centre. The Academy's first foundation course is also being held today and tomorrow during the Business of IP Asia Forum.
 
     The Acting Secretary for Commerce and Economic Development, Dr Bernard Chan, attended the Academy's opening ceremony at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre today. Addressing the opening ceremony, Dr Chan said, "The National 15th Five-Year Plan Outline explicitly supports Hong Kong in deepening its development as a regional IP trading centre. Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan also sets out the establishment of an IP academy to systemically nurture talent for IP-intensive industries, equipping them with knowledge and skills in IP creation, protection, management, financing, utilisation and commercialisation, thereby further advancing Hong Kong's IP ecosystem. Today's launch of the Academy marks an important step in implementing this initiative."
 
     He added that IP is not only about legal protection and rights registration, but is also closely connected with the commercialisation of research outcomes, brand development, licensing and trading. He said he looked forward to the Academy bringing together industry expertise and connecting with international resources to nurture talent for Hong Kong's development as a regional IP trading centre, and make greater contributions to the country's innovation-driven development.
 
     The Academy was jointly established by the Intellectual Property Department and the Vocational Training Council (VTC). The Government earmarked $52 million in the 2026-27 Budget to support the Academy's establishment and its first two years of operation. It is expected to provide training for around 2 000 participants during the two-year pilot period. To address the needs of the innovation and technology, cultural and creative, business and professional services sectors, the Academy will establish a multilevel on-the-job training pathway ranging from foundation to advanced levels, and progressively develop suitable training courses into certified courses and Qualifications Framework-recognised programmes.
 
     The Academy's first course, IP101 Intellectual Property Basics, lasts one and a half days and is delivered by speakers with relevant professional knowledge and practical experiences. It covers different types of IP, including trade marks, copyright, patents, designs and trade secrets, as well as the basic concepts of IP trading. The course helps participants understand the rights and responsibilities of IP owners and users, and apply what they have learnt to business operations.
 
     Other guests attending today's ceremony included the Chairman of the VTC, Mr Jeffrey Lam; Judge of the Court of First Instance of the High Court Mr Justice David Lok; the Permanent Secretary for Commerce and Economic Development, Ms Angela Lee; Deputy Director General of the World Intellectual Property Organization Dr Shen Changyu; the Director of Intellectual Property, Mr David Wong; the Chairman of the Steering Committee on the Hong Kong Intellectual Property Academy Pilot Programme, Professor Sunny Lee; and the Acting Executive Director of the VTC, Ms Gladys Yam.

item.title: Inspection of aquatic products imported from Japan
item.description:
In response to the Japanese Government's plan to discharge nuclear-contaminated water at the Fukushima Nuclear Power Station, the Director of Food and Environmental Hygiene issued a Food Safety Order which prohibits all aquatic products, sea salt and seaweeds originating from the 10 metropolis/prefectures, namely Tokyo, Fukushima, Ibaraki, Miyagi, Chiba, Gunma, Tochigi, Niigata, Nagano and Saitama, from being imported into and supplied in Hong Kong.
 
     For other Japanese aquatic products, sea salt and seaweeds that are not prohibited from being imported into Hong Kong, the Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department is conducting comprehensive radiological tests to verify that the radiation levels of these products do not exceed the guideline levels before they are allowed to be supplied in the market.
 
     From noon on November 18 to noon today (November 19), the CFS conducted tests on the radiological levels of 144 food samples imported from Japan, which were of the "aquatic and related products, seaweeds and sea salt" category. No sample was found to have exceeded the safety limit. Details can be found on the CFS's thematic website titled "Control Measures on Foods Imported from Japan" (www.cfs.gov.hk/english/programme/programme_rafs/programme_rafs_fc_01_30_Nuclear_Event_and_Food_Safety.html).
 
     In parallel, the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) has also tested 50 samples of local catch for radiological levels. All the samples passed the tests. Details can be found on the AFCD's website (www.afcd.gov.hk/english/fisheries/Radiological_testing/Radiological_Test.html).
 
     The Hong Kong Observatory (HKO) has also enhanced the environmental monitoring of the local waters. No anomaly has been detected so far. For details, please refer to the HKO's website (www.hko.gov.hk/en/radiation/monitoring/seawater.html).
 
     From August 24, 2023, to noon today, the CFS and the AFCD have conducted tests on the radiological levels of 276 546 samples of food imported from Japan (including 172 048 samples of aquatic and related products, seaweeds and sea salt) and 58 814 samples of local catch respectively. All the samples passed the tests.

item.title: Speech by Acting SCED at APEC Workshop on Leveraging IP Financing for Innovative Enterprises: Current Landscape, Key Challenges and Way Forward (English only)
item.description:
Following is the speech by the Acting Secretary for Commerce and Economic Development, Dr Bernard Chan, at the APEC (Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation) Workshop on Leveraging IP (Intellectual Property) Financing for Innovative Enterprises: Current Landscape, Key Challenges and Way Forward today (November 19):

Distinguished guests, speakers, delegates, ladies and gentlemen,

     Good afternoon. Welcome to Hong Kong, China, and to this APEC workshop on leveraging IP financing for innovative enterprises.

     Let me begin by thanking the APEC IP Rights Experts Group and our co-sponsoring economies, Chile, China, Korea and Singapore, for their support in making this workshop possible. As China hosts APEC this year, we are delighted to contribute to regional co-operation through this workshop, which is being held alongside the Business of IP Asia Forum.

     Innovation creates value. But turning that value into finance is not always straightforward. For many innovative enterprises, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and start-ups, patents, trade marks and other IP assets are important sources of competitive advantages underpinning their companies' worth. Yet these businesses may struggle to secure financing when they lack traditional tangible collateral.

     There are several challenges to overcome, including complex valuation, limited market reference data and difficulties in realising IP value. Addressing them can help enterprises access capital to develop new products, to enter new markets and to commercialise their research and creative outcomes.

     For Hong Kong, our strengths as an international financial centre, supported by our professional services, provide a strong foundation for developing IP financing and advancing our role as a regional IP trading centre.

     Last December, our bureau, the Commerce and Economic Development Bureau, together with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Intellectual Property Department, launched the IP Financing Sandbox. It brings together banks, enterprises and professional services organisations to test IP-based financing arrangements in a collaborative, risk-controlled environment.

     In September this year, we announced the first seven pilot cases that had successfully completed credit approval. They cover the electronics, construction, toy manufacturing and medical device sectors, involving IP assets comprising patents and trademarks, with loan amounts ranging from $1 million to $39 million.

     These are encouraging first steps. By taking account of IP asset value, participating banks have offered greater flexibility regarding loan amounts and financing terms, while gaining valuable experiences in valuation, credit assessment and risk management.

     Practical testing must go hand in hand with stronger support. In September, we also launched the two-year Pilot Patent Valuation Support Scheme through the Hong Kong Technology and Innovation Support Centre. It helps eligible SMEs meet the cost of professional valuation of their patents and other IP assets, with qualitative patent evaluation provided as a complementary tool where appropriate.

     Better information helps enterprises demonstrate the economic value of their assets and enables financiers to assess opportunities and risks. It supports, rather than replaces, commercial judgement and prudent risk assessment.

     People are equally important. Later today, we will launch the Hong Kong IP Academy to provide more systematic, practical IP training across industries. We need enterprises that understand and manage their IP strategically, alongside professionals who can assess its commercial potential. By equipping both groups with the necessary knowledge and skills, training helps build these complementary capabilities.

     Looking ahead, the value of a pilot lies not only in the transactions it facilitates, but also in the knowledge, confidence and working relationships it builds.

     Government can facilitate testing and strengthen support measures. Banks and professional services providers bring commercial expertise and risk assessment. Enterprises must prepare and manage their IP assets to support their business objectives. Progress depends on effective collaboration among all parties.

     We will consolidate our experiences from the Sandbox and market feedback to explore wider participation, facilitate more pilot cases and enhance valuation processes.

     This is also where APEC co-operation can make a difference. Our economies have different legal frameworks and market conditions; no single model fits all. By exchanging practical lessons, sharing experiences and learning from one another, we can each develop approaches suited to our circumstances.

     Ladies and gentlemen, let us build on today's exchanges to turn shared knowledge into practical financing opportunities. Together, we can help more enterprises bring their innovations to market, creating new sources of growth and contributing to a more dynamic and innovative Asia-Pacific economy.

     I wish you all a productive workshop. Thank you so much.

item.title: Remarks by CE at media session in Shenzhen (with photo/video)
item.description:
The Chief Executive, Mr John Lee, met the media in Shenzhen this afternoon (November 19) during his attendance at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting and other related activities. Following are Mr Lee's remarks:

Reporter: My first question is, what do you see, or expect to be, Hong Kong's biggest achievement and takeaway at this year's event? Hong Kong is serving its dual role as a "super connector" and a "super value-adder". How would you explain this important concept to our global audience, especially in terms of the SAR's integration into the overall national development of China and the Greater Bay Area?

Chief Executive: We have been actively participating. I think we have achieved five results. 

     First, contributing Hong Kong's strength by actively participating in and supporting our country's successful hosting of the APEC meetings. The Hong Kong SAR (Special Administrative Region) has a dual role on this occasion. Hong Kong, China is an APEC member, and I am, at the same time, an official of China, our country. Therefore, we should take an active role in assisting our country's successful hosting of this year's APEC meetings. Therefore, Hong Kong, China actively attended and organised meetings and workshops, and launched a series of capacity-building projects. For this week's APEC Economic Leaders' Week, Hong Kong has sent its largest-ever delegation of over 50 members. 

     Second, deepening exchanges with APEC member economies. APEC member economies are Hong Kong's important trading partners, accounting for 87 per cent of Hong Kong's external trade. Through APEC meetings and events, I exchanged views with leaders of various economies. Through bilateral meetings and engagements, I met with the leaders of seven economies: Malaysia, Vietnam, Brunei, Thailand, Chile, Peru and Singapore to strengthen ties and discuss issues of mutual concern. 

     Third, consolidating relations with ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) member states. Seven ASEAN member states are APEC members. ASEAN is Hong Kong's second-largest trading partner. The APEC meetings provided me with the opportunity to meet with five ASEAN leaders at bilateral meetings and engagements to further consolidate our relations. 

     Fourth, further exploring emerging markets. The Hong Kong SAR Government is actively expanding Hong Kong's economic and trade network, and expanding and exploring different markets, especially on strengthening ties with emerging markets and economies with growth potential. Yesterday, the President of Chile and I jointly witnessed the signing of the Working Holiday Scheme agreement between Hong Kong and Chile. 

     Fifth, telling good stories of the Greater Bay Area (GBA) and Hong Kong. The successful hosting of APEC meetings in Shenzhen, a core city of the Greater Bay Area, fully demonstrated the GBA's strength and charm as a window for the country's high-standard opening up. At the APEC CEO Summit on Tuesday, I seized the opportunity to promote the development opportunities of the GBA and Hong Kong's unique advantages, and I also discussed GBA opportunities with participating leaders. 

     My takeaway is that Hong Kong's development resonates with our country's development. As an international city and international financial centre, we can serve the country's needs with our unique advantages and what Hong Kong does best. We are pressing ahead with four centres development and one hub development, contributing to our country's high-quality development. Therefore, we shall actively integrate with and serve our national development, and at the same time, we will strengthen our connectivity with the international world.

     On connectivity, Hong Kong can continue to leverage our unique advantages under the "one country, two systems" principle to play an active role as a "super connector" and "super value-adder". We can make full use of APEC and other international platforms to showcase the HKSAR as an international hub. The 2026 APEC Finance Ministers' Meeting in the HKSAR actually demonstrated our unique advantage in this regard. We can also expand the global trade and investment network. Through our 15 overseas ETOs (Economic and Trade Offices), together with Hong Kong Trade Development Council and Invest Hong Kong offices, our network covers 68 cities and 129 countries. We will deepen engagement with emerging economies in ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations), the Middle East, Central Asia and South America, pursue early RCEP (Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership) accession, and aim at reaching more free trade agreements and investment promotion and protection agreements. I think we can also leverage Hong Kong's status as an international centre to contribute to the country's high-quality development. We will press ahead with the development of the "four centres and one hub" to serve the country's high-level opening up. 

     As regards deepening our integration into national development, first of all, I think we can deepen Greater Bay Area development through hard and soft connectivity and connectivity of hearts, and take forward the Northern Metropolis development for integrating into national development. Second, we can contribute to Belt and Road co-operation. Third, we can, through the GoGlobal Task Force (Task Force on Supporting Mainland Enterprises in Going Global), support Mainland enterprises in leveraging Hong Kong's world-class professional services and extensive global network, and using Hong Kong as a springboard to expand into global markets. Thank you.

(Please also refer to the Chinese portion of the remarks.)

item.title: Voters to follow voting procedures in 2026 Election Committee Subsector Ordinary Elections to be held this Sunday (with video)
item.description:
The 2026 Election Committee Subsector Ordinary Elections will be held this Sunday (November 22) with polling hours from 9am to 6pm. The Registration and Electoral Office (REO) reminds voters/authorised representatives (ARs) concerned to follow the instructions on their poll card and bring the original of their valid Hong Kong identity (HKID) card to vote at their designated polling station.

     A spokesman for the REO said today (November 19), "In accordance with the law, only registered voters/ARs in the 2026 final register of voters for Election Committee subsectors who belong to the 31 contested subsectors are eligible to vote on the polling day. The voters/ARs of these subsectors may use 'iAM Smart' or the voter registration website (vr.gov.hk) to log in to the Online Voter Information Enquiry System to check polling information such as the name and address of their designated polling station and its location on the map, the polling hours, as well as the Introduction to Candidates. They can also call the election hotline (2891 1001) for enquiries. A video introducing the voting procedures has been uploaded to the election website (www.elections.gov.hk)."

     On the polling day, a total of 856 candidates will contest 723 seats in 31 subsectors. Five ordinary polling stations (OPSs) located at Harbour Road Sports Centre, Kowloon Park Sports Centre, Tsuen Wan Sports Centre, Tiu Keng Leng Sports Centre and Che Kung Temple Sports Centre, and two dedicated polling stations located at Happy Valley Police Station and Shek Pik Prison will be set up for voters/ARs of the contested subsectors to cast their votes.

Polling arrangements

     The OPSs will make use of the Electronic Poll Register (EPR) System to issue ballot papers for the elections. Voters/ARs must produce the original of their valid HKID card at the ballot paper issuing desk in the polling station. The polling staff will scan the HKID card of the voters/ARs using a tablet of the EPR System to verify their identity and issue the ballot paper(s) upon verification.

     When marking the ballot paper, voters/ARs must use the pen provided at the polling station to shade the ovals to the left of their chosen candidates' names. The number of chosen candidates should be no more than the prescribed number of seats to be elected by the relevant subsector, or the ballot paper will be regarded as invalid.

     The spokesman said, "Ballot paper checking machines will be available at the polling stations for voters/ARs to check whether they have marked their ballot paper(s) properly in accordance with electoral laws. The ballot paper checking machines will not record or count choices marked on the ballot papers. After checking, the voters/ARs should turn the ballot paper so the marked side faces down and put the unfolded ballot paper directly into the ballot box. It is in principle alright for voters/ARs to bring along a piece of paper listing the names or numbers of the candidates of their choice for easy reference when marking the ballot papers. Nevertheless, voters/ARs should bear in mind that they should not show the paper to other people inside the polling station and they should take the paper with them when leaving the polling station. Otherwise, the voters/ARs concerned may violate the electoral laws," the spokesman said.

     Based on the principles of the autonomy of voting and secrecy of votes, it is prohibited under the law to have anyone (even the voter/AR's relative or friend) accompany or assist voters to cast their vote(s). If necessary, voters/ARs may, in accordance with the law, ask the Presiding Officer or his/her deputy to mark the ballot paper on the voters/ARs' behalf in the presence of a member of the polling staff as witness. It is an offence for any voter/AR to disturb others, use electronic devices for communication, take photographs, or make video or audio recordings at a polling station.

     The spokesman said that the introduction booklets on candidates printed by the REO will be displayed at all polling stations for reference by voters/ARs.

Special arrangements at polling stations

     Two queues will be set up at the polling stations. One queue is for people aged 70 or above, pregnant women and persons who are unable to queue for a long time due to physical conditions, while another queue is for other voters/ARs. The Presiding Officers will flexibly deploy ballot paper issuing desks depending on the queuing situation.

     A certain area outside each polling station will be designated as a no canvassing zone to ensure that voters/ARs can gain access to the polling stations without interference. No one is allowed to canvass for votes or conduct "de-facto canvassing" such as making hand gestures and greetings in the no canvassing zone. A no staying zone will also be designated in the vicinity of the entrance and exit of a polling station. No one is allowed to stay in the no staying zone.

     Enquiries about the elections on the polling day can be made to the election hotline at 2891 1001, which will operate from 8.30am to 6.30pm that day. A complaint hotline (2827 7251/3707 0188) will be in service from 8.30am to 7pm that day to handle complaints about breaches of electoral rules or guidelines.

Counting arrangements

     Central counting will be adopted for the elections. Once the poll is closed, the ballot boxes will be delivered to the Central Counting Station (CCS) at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre for counting. Candidates, election agents and counting agents may enter the CCS to observe the count at designated areas of the counting zone. Members of the public and media may also enter the CCS to observe the count but they are not allowed to enter the counting zone. A notice setting out the maximum capacity of members of the public in the public area will be displayed outside the CCS.

     Once the counting of votes of a subsector is completed and verified by the REO, the Returning Officer will make known the counting and election results to the candidates and their agents present at the tables for determination of questionable ballot papers at the CCS. Also, the elected candidates will be invited to receive applause on the stage of the Media Centre (MC). The election results will be displayed outside the MC and published via press releases and the election website.

     For enquiries, please call the election hotline on 2891 1001 or visit the election website for more information on the elections.

item.title: EDB announces Study Subsidy Scheme for Designated Professions/Sectors for 2027/28 cohort - sub-degree programmes

The Education Bureau (EDB) announced today (November 19) that the Study Subsidy Scheme for Designated Professions/Sectors (SSSDP) will subsidise a total of 2 196 places in 35 sub-degree programmes of five post-secondary institutions for the cohort to be admitted in the 2027/28 academic year.

     These 35 designated sub-degree programmes fall under seven disciplines that have been identified as having keen manpower demand, namely architecture and engineering, computer science, creative industries, health care, sports and recreation, testing and certification, and tourism and hospitality. The programmes and number of subsidised places (see Annex) are determined by the EDB in consultation with relevant policy bureaux and departments.

     In the 2027/28 academic year, the annual subsidy amounts for laboratory-based programmes and non-laboratory-based programmes will be $40,730 and $23,390 respectively. The subsidy amounts are applicable to both new and continuing eligible students. The subsidy is tenable for the normal duration of the programmes concerned. Subsidised students will pay a tuition fee with the subsidy applied. Students in need may still apply for student financial assistance from the Student Finance Office of the Working Family and Student Financial Assistance Agency in respect of the actual amount of tuition fee payable.

     The SSSDP aims to subsidise students to pursue designated full-time locally accredited self-financing undergraduate and sub-degree programmes in selected disciplines with a view to nurturing talent for industries with keen human resource demand. The designated undergraduate programmes in the 2027/28 academic year, including the number of subsidised places and the subsidy amounts concerned, were announced on September 21.
