item.title: SFST showcases Hong Kong's financial strengths in Luxembourg (with photos)
item.description:
The Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury, Mr Christopher Hui, on November 18 (Luxembourg time) embarked on the second leg of his European duty visit in Luxembourg where he met with multiple government officials, financial regulators, banks and financial institutions.

     He began the day by calling on Luxembourg's Ministry of Finance, where he met with the Secretary General and Director of the Treasury, Mr Bob Kieffer. Highlighting Hong Kong's strategic direction under its inaugural Five-Year Plan, Mr Hui stated that the Plan not only reinforces the city's standing as an international financial centre, a global offshore Renminbi hub, an international asset and wealth management centre, and an international risk management centre, but also brings predictability to investors and businesses with concrete policy directions. With common strengths and interest in wealth management as well as green and digital finance, Mr Hui said Luxembourg and Hong Kong are well-positioned as strategic partners to expand collaboration in reinforcing their respective roles as safe harbours for capital in Europe and Asia. Furthermore, Hong Kong can serve as a premier gateway for Luxembourg to access the vast opportunities in the Chinese Mainland.

     To gain a better grasp of Luxembourg's financial landscape, Mr Hui met with the Chief Executive Officer of Luxembourg for Finance (LFF), Mr Tom Théobald, and the Chief Executive Officer of the Association of the Luxembourg Fund Industry (ALFI), Mr Serge Weyland, followed by a roundtable luncheon with key representatives from Luxembourg's banking and wealth management sectors. The ALFI represents Luxembourg's asset management and investment fund community while LFF is the public-private partnership between the Luxembourg Government and the Luxembourg Financial Industry Federation, PROFIL.

     Mr Hui told the parties that predictability and stability are the hallmark strengths of Hong Kong's financial environment. He added that the Government strives to optimise the financial ecosystem through enhanced facilitation, including the introduction of legislation to enhance the preferential tax regimes for funds, single family offices and carried interest, as well as the real estate investment trust (REIT) regime to boost the competitiveness and liquidity of the REIT market.

     He also mentioned the encouraging progress of Hong Kong's commodity market since its inclusion as an approved delivery point by the London Metal Exchange in January 2025. The total storage area has already exceeded 74 000 square metres, with non-ferrous metals storage exceeding 67 000 tonnes as of end-October, which represents very encouraging progress. The Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited is also striving to launch a pilot project for tokenised warehouse-receipt financing in collaboration with designated banks in 2027 to promote the use of commodity inventories as collateral by enterprises in securing liquidity.

     He later visited the Luxembourg Stock Exchange, a leading European stock exchange specialising in international listings with a focus on sustainable finance and cross-border capital market services. Mr Hui shared with its Deputy Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, Mr Pierre Schoonbroodt, and other senior management the latest moves of Hong Kong to enhance stock market liquidity, including promoting dual primary and secondary listing of overseas enterprises in Hong Kong, and advancing the securities market to a T+1 settlement cycle.

     In the afternoon, Mr Hui met with the Director of the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), Mr Marco Zwick. The CSSF is a public institution responsible for supervising the professionals and products of the Luxembourg financial sector. Mr Hui echoed the importance of adhering to international standards to ensure the smooth operation of the market and robust investor protection, emphasising that Hong Kong also has a strong regulatory framework in place as the core pillar to support its vibrant and stable financial market. 

     During a meeting with Vice-President of the European Investment Bank Dr Marko Primorac, Mr Hui updated him on Hong Kong's latest initiatives to strengthen its green finance ecosystem, including two cross-boundary pilots completed by Core Climate: one enabling Hong Kong enterprises to purchase green electricity certificates from the Chinese Mainland, and the other testing settlement of carbon emission allowances. 

     Mr Hui also paid a courtesy call on the Chargé d'Affaires ad interim of the Chinese Embassy in Luxembourg, Mr Zhu Weiye, to provide him with an update on the latest financial developments in Hong Kong.

     He will head to Brussels, Belgium, on November 19 (Luxembourg time) to continue his duty visit.

item.title: Opening remarks by PSITI at "The Economics of Open Development: The Case for Open-Source AI" organised by United Nations Office for Digital and Emerging Technologies (English only) (with photo)
item.description:
Following are the opening remarks by the Permanent Secretary for Innovation, Technology and Industry, Mr Kevin Choi, at "The Economics of Open Development: The Case for Open-Source AI" organised by the United Nations Office for Digital and Emerging Technologies today (November 19):

Dr Snene (Senior Advisor to the United Nations Secretary-General's Special Envoy on Digital and Emerging Technologies, Dr Mehdi Snene), Professor Shum (Vice-President and Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Research) of the University of Hong Kong, Professor Anderson Shum), distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen,

     Good morning. It is a great honour to join you all at this workshop. First, I would like to thank the United Nations Office for Digital and Emerging Technologies, the United Nations International Computing Centre and all partners for bringing us together. Building on the first phase of the United Nations Blueprint for National AI and Data Strategies, today's discussion on the Public AI Stack addresses an important question: how economies can build and sustain AI services on shared, open foundations. 

     This focus on open-source AI resonates with our country's Global AI Governance Initiative, which calls for global collaboration to foster the sound development of AI, share AI knowledge and make AI technologies available to the public under open-source terms.

     Indeed, open-source AI lowers barriers to innovation, avoids duplicated investment and widens access to AI technologies. In support of this national initiative, Hong Kong is well placed to contribute. Under "one country, two systems", we combine close connections with the Mainland's innovation ecosystem with international networks, strong research capabilities and the free flow of information, capital and talent. These strengths enable us to serve as a bridge between the Mainland and the world, connecting researchers, developers and enterprises across borders to develop, adapt and share open-source AI.

     Building on these strengths, our First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region advances the AI+ Initiative through the twin directions of "industries for AI" and "AI for industries". We are pursuing AI development alongside governance, while strengthening collaboration between research institutions and industry. For open-source AI to deliver lasting value, access to technology must be matched by computing resources, research expertise, usable data and responsible deployment.

     We begin with computing power. Hong Kong's overall computing capacity has reached 5 000 PFLOPS (peta-floating point operations per second), including 3 000 PFLOPS from Cyberport's AI Supercomputing Centre. To make this capacity more accessible, the Government launched the AI Subsidy Scheme in 2024, supporting local universities, research institutes and enterprises in pursuing research breakthroughs. To support future growth, the Sandy Ridge Data Facility Cluster, now under construction, is expected to provide an additional 180 000 PFLOPS by 2032, equivalent to 36 times our current capacity.  

     To turn this infrastructure into innovation, we are strengthening research and its links with industry. The Hong Kong AI Research and Development Institute, established earlier this year and preparing to commence operations, will steer upstream research, accelerate commercialisation, advise on AI governance and facilitate international exchanges. It will strengthen the links between scientific discovery and practical application, helping research outcomes deliver benefits for industries and the community.  

     International collaboration further strengthens these capabilities. Our AIR@InnoHK research cluster, dedicated to AI and robotics, brings together 16 laboratories and around 1 200 experts from leading local and global institutions. Within this cluster, the Hong Kong Generative AI Research and Development Centre, established in 2023 with government support, has leveraged open-source foundations to develop locally trained large language models tailored to Hong Kong's languages and application scenarios.
       
     As these capabilities grow, governance must keep pace. Under the co-ordination of the Chief Secretary for Administration, our AI risk-governance strategy addresses issues including criminal misuse, protection of minors, application safety, legal liability, AI agents and employment impacts. Our Ethical Artificial Intelligence Framework and Hong Kong Generative Artificial Intelligence Technical and Application Guideline also provide practical guidance for responsible adoption. Such safeguards are equally important for open-source AI, where openness must go hand in hand with safety, accountability and trust.  

     Hong Kong's contribution is therefore to connect capabilities: research with industry, shared technology with local needs, and innovation with governance. As this workshop considers the Public AI Stack, we look forward to exchanging experiences and exploring collaboration with partners. By combining shared technological foundations with local capabilities and appropriate safeguards, we can turn AI potential into sustainable services and tangible public benefit. Thank you.

item.title: Speech by FS at 2026 Business of Intellectual Property Asia Forum (English only) (with photos/video)
item.description:
​Following is the speech by the Financial Secretary, Mr Paul Chan, at the 2026 Business of Intellectual Property Asia Forum today (November 19):

Deputy Director-General Shen Changyu (Deputy Director General of the World Intellectual Property Organisation), Deputy Head Jiang Tung (Deputy Head of the Patent Office of the China National Intellectual Property Administration), Director General Wang Zhicheng (Director General of the Copyright Department of the Publicity Department of the Communist Party of China Central Committee), Sophia (Executive Director of the Hong Kong Trade Development Council, Ms Sophia Chong), distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen,

     Good morning.

     It is my pleasure to welcome you to the 16th Business of Intellectual Property Asia Forum. To our guests from the Mainland and overseas, a very warm welcome to Hong Kong.

     The theme of this year, "Powering Commercial Success through IP and Innovation", rests on a simple premise: that ideas have become the main source of commercial value. Let me begin with how far that is now true.

A world built on intangibles

     For most of economic history, wealth was something that could be counted, weighed or fenced in: land, factories, ships. Today, the most valuable things a company owns are often those that cannot be seen.

     Across the economies tracked by WIPO, the World Intellectual Property Organisation, investment in intangible assets such as software, data, brands and know-how passed US$10 trillion for the first time last year. Since 2008, it has grown more than three times as fast as investment in buildings and machinery. At the same time, artificial intelligence will only accelerate the shift, for its lasting value will lie less in data centres than in the intangible assets built on top of them.

Asia: from creating to earning

     Much of this story is being written in Asia, where seven in ten of the world's patent applications are now filed. Our country is the largest source of international patent applications, and WIPO ranks the cluster running from Shenzhen through Hong Kong to Guangzhou as the world's leading innovation cluster. And from Korean drama to Chinese designer toys and creative brands born in this region are winning fans on every continent.

     Yet creating IP (intellectual property) and monetising it are two very different things. Most economies in our region still pay more for the use of IP than they receive. Asia has learned how to create. The task for the coming decade is to capture more of the value of what it creates.

Four challenges

     So what stands in the way? Let me touch briefly on three challenges that this audience knows well. IP is hard to see: some 80 per cent of the intangible value of the world's listed companies do not appear on balance sheet. IP is hard to finance: a bank can visit a factory, but it cannot visit an idea. And IP is hard to trade across borders, because rights stop at the border while business does not.

     Asia is already testing the answers. Mainland banks extended close to RMB 300 billion in loans secured on IP last year, and in Korea IP finance has more than doubled in five years. The lesson is that lenders need credible valuation, some risk sharing, and a market in which IP can be sold if a loan goes wrong.

     AI now adds a fourth challenge by changing the terms on which IP is created and used. Who owns what a machine that helps to create? On what terms may creative works be used to train a model? No jurisdiction can claim to have settled the matter. Last week in Geneva, WIPO's Director General, Mr Daren Tang, put it very well.  The question, he said, cannot simply be who has the legal power to say no. We must also ask how to create workable ways for people to say yes. Asia, a leading producer of both technology and content, has every reason to help build them.

Hong Kong's contribution

     Ladies and gentlemen, no single economy can meet these challenges alone. Let me turn to what Hong Kong is doing, and where we go next.

     The National 15th Five-Year Plan supports Hong Kong in deepening its development as a regional IP trading centre. Our own First Five-Year Plan sets out how, including by bringing finance and IP closer together, and by making it less costly, and easier, to hold and trade IP here.

     We have started with where the need is the greatest, bank credit for smaller firms. Our IP Financing Sandbox, launched with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority last December, has seen its first seven loans approved. The numbers may be small, but banks, valuers and borrowers are discovering together what makes IP bankable. The next phase of the initiative will draw in more participants. And a new pilot scheme will help smaller firms obtain professional valuations of their patents, in line with the national standard. Our task now is to move from sandbox to scale.

     Bank credit is only the first link. As companies grow, they need investors who can price ideas. For example, since 2018, more than 90 biotechnology companies have listed in Hong Kong under rules written for firms yet to earn revenue. Together, they have raised over US$19 billion on the strength of their science, including their patents. Some of the medicines now being licensed to the world came from companies financed in this way.

     None of this works without sound foundations. A patent is only as strong as the examination behind it. So we are expanding our team of examiners. By 2030, we aim to examine applications in major technology fields in-house.

     A deal is only as attractive as its cost. So our patent box allows qualifying IP profits to be taxed at just five per cent. And a Bill now before the Legislative Council will widen tax deductions for buying and licensing IP.

     An agreement is only as reliable as its enforcement. So IP disputes can be settled here by arbitration or mediation, under a bilingual common law system that international parties know well.

     Hong Kong's particular role is to connect. Last year, a patent granted in Hong Kong helped to back a securitisation listed in Shenzhen, the first time IP from outside the Mainland has been used in this way. It was small, but it showed that an idea protected on one side of the boundary can raise capital on the other. The traffic can run both ways. We also want Mainland enterprises to use Hong Kong to take their IP to the world. 

     Above all, a market for ideas depends on people. It takes professionals fluent in both IP and business to value a patent, negotiate a licence or lend against either. This afternoon we will launch the Hong Kong IP Academy to train more of them. Working with the Vocational Training Council, the Academy will offer structured, recognised training to practitioners in innovation and technology, the creative industries, commerce and professional services.

     On AI, we are still listening: to creators, to developers and to the experience of others. What Hong Kong can offer is a place to test ideas. And we will share our experience with our partners on the Mainland and around the world.

Closing 

     Ladies and gentlemen, this Forum is where much of that sharing takes place. My thanks to the Hong Kong Trade Development Council, our co-organiser, and to all our speakers and partners.

     I began with the things we cannot see. Our shared task is to make them easier to see, to finance and to trade, and to keep our rules fit for an age of AI, so that a good idea born anywhere in Asia can travel the world and prove its worth. I wish you all a rewarding Forum and enjoyable stay in Hong Kong. Thank you.

item.title: London ETO promotes I&T opportunities under Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan at Slush 2026 in Finland (with photos)
item.description:
​The Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in London (London ETO), in collaboration with Invest Hong Kong (InvestHK) and the Hong Kong Trade Development Council (HKTDC) under the Economic and Trade Express platform, as well as the Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks Corporation (HKSTP), organised a seminar themed "Next Stop Asia: Scaling your I&T Business through Hong Kong" at Slush 2026 in Helsinki, Finland, on November 18 (Helsinki time). The seminar showcased Hong Kong's innovation and technology (I&T) development and the opportunities it offers to Nordic start-ups seeking to expand into Asian markets.
     
     Speaking at the seminar, the Director-General of the London ETO, Miss Fiona Chau, highlighted Hong Kong's role as a launch pad for Nordic businesses seeking to expand into Asia. She said that Hong Kong connects international talent, technology and capital with opportunities in the Chinese Mainland, particularly the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) and the wider Asian market.
     
     Miss Chau outlined Hong Kong's vision of developing into an international I&T centre under the First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (2026-2030). She highlighted the development of three major I&T parks and five key research and development institutions, supported by substantial investment, to strengthen Hong Kong's I&T ecosystem and accelerate the translation of research and innovation into commercial opportunities.
     
     She also introduced the Northern Metropolis (NM) as a major development project that will create new opportunities for innovation development and cross-boundary collaboration. She highlighted the complementary roles of the Hong Kong Park of the Hetao Shenzhen-Hong Kong Science and Technology Innovation Co-operation Zone - the Hong Kong-Shenzhen Innovation and Technology Park (HSITP) and San Tin Technopole in the NM in supporting research, commercialisation and industrial development. She also outlined the distinctive cross-boundary collaboration model of "one river, two banks; one zone, two parks" adopted by the HSITP and its neighbouring Shenzhen Park. This model offers Nordic enterprises valuable opportunities to establish a presence in Hong Kong, leverage its unique advantages under "one country, two systems", collaborate with research institutions and I&T partners in both Hong Kong and Shenzhen, and tap into the GBA's technology and manufacturing capabilities.
     
     The Head of Innovation and Technology and Life and Health Sciences of InvestHK, Mr Andy Wong, also delivered a presentation at the seminar titled "Hong Kong as a Gateway to Unlock Business Opportunities in China and Wider Asia (from a Tech Venture Perspective)". Moreover, representatives of the HKTDC, the HKSTP and two Nordic-based companies shared their insights on the latest developments in Hong Kong's I&T sector, the opportunities available to overseas companies and the sector's future prospects during a fireside chat. Drawing on their experiences and expertise, the speakers also discussed practical considerations for Nordic start-ups looking to enter the Hong Kong market, identify suitable partners and further expand into the wider Asian market.
     
     The London ETO will continue to work closely with InvestHK, the HKTDC and the HKSTP to promote Hong Kong's I&T development and foster collaboration between I&T companies in Hong Kong and the Nordic region.
     
     Slush is an annual global start-up event held in Helsinki, bringing together start-up founders, investors and other members of the technology and entrepreneurial ecosystem from around the world. The event provides a platform for networking, sharing insights and connecting start-ups with potential investors and business partners.

item.title: Business of Design Week 2026 and DesignInspire open (with photos)
item.description:

     Speaking today at the opening ceremony of BODW and at the networking reception of DesignInspire, the Secretary for Culture, Sports and Tourism, Miss Rosanna Law, said that both events showcase Hong Kong's unique strength in connecting creative talent from around the world and in fostering cross-cultural exchange and business collaboration. item.title: FEHD wins two more accolades in Best Public Toilet Award
item.description:
A spokesman for the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) said today (November 18) that the department is pleased to learn that two public toilets under its management have won the gold and bronze awards this year in the annual Hong Kong's Best Public Toilet Award organised by the Hong Kong Toilet Association.

     The Gold Award winner, the Lei Yue Mun (Ling Nam Sun Tsuen) Public Toilet in Kwun Tong District, adopted the winning design concept from the PT 2.0 Public Toilet Design Competition. Inspired by "siphonophores", it features a modular structure with flexible combinations that seamlessly adapts to different terrains and environments, infusing creativity into public facilities. Upholding a "human-centric" design philosophy, the public toilet has a spacious interior, accessible and universal toilets equipped with automatic doors, and a water dispenser outside for the convenience of both residents and tourists. A smart monitoring system has also been installed to monitor odours in real time and send automated alerts, enhancing hygiene standards and management efficiency, while a contactless feedback system collects user comments to inform service improvements and future planning. Furthermore, its accessible toilet is fitted with the Smart Accident Detection System to detect falls and abnormal prolonged inactivity, enabling timely assistance.

     As for the Bronze Award winner, the Aberdeen Main Road Public Toilet in Southern District, following refurbishment, it features a warm earth-toned colour palette paired with clean, crisp lines, showcasing a unique modern aesthetic. It is equipped with facilities designed for children and the elderly to cater to the needs of users of different ages.

     The spokesman said, "The FEHD has been adopting a multi-pronged approach, including the introduction of new technologies, to enhance the facilities, management, and hygiene standards of the public toilets under its purview, while ensuring designs cater to the needs of diverse users. The repeated accolades won by the FEHD's public toilets reflect recognition of its ongoing efforts to enhance public toilet services, which is truly encouraging. Keeping public toilets clean and comfortable over the long term also relies on the dedicated efforts of frontline staff in cleaning and management. The department thanks them for their hard work and contributions."

     The FEHD earlier noticed odours emanating from certain areas inside the Chai Wan Kok Public Toilet in Tsuen Wan District and immediately notified the relevant department to arrange for repairs. The department has set up mobile toilets nearby and will step up the cleaning of the mobile toilets until the repair works are completed and requested the relevant department to expedite the repair of damaged facilities. Furthermore, to improve the facilities at the Tai Kiu Tsuen Public Toilet and the Tung Chau Street Public Toilet, the FEHD has included both public toilets in its refurbishment programme, requiring contractors to step up cleaning efforts, and will closely monitor their service performance.

     Currently, the FEHD manages over 800 public toilets, and has in recent years actively partnered with the Architectural Services Department to take forward the Enhanced Public Toilet Refurbishment Programme. Before the implementation of the programme in 2019, refurbishment had already commenced for about 110 public toilets. Of the remaining approximately 700 public toilets covered under the programme, works have currently been rolled out for nearly 85 per cent, with works for over 250 already successfully completed. The department aims to commence refurbishment works for the approximately 110 remaining public toilets by the end of 2028.

     Adopting the recommendations of a consultancy study report by the City University of Hong Kong, the FEHD has, since 2023, implemented a male-to-female toilet compartment ratio standard of 1:2.32 in newly built or refurbished public toilets with high usage rates. For public toilets with low usage rates or in remote locations, flexible adjustments will be made depending on site circumstances, spatial constraints, and practical operational needs.

     The spokesman stated that the FEHD has always been dedicated to improving environmental hygiene. Going forward, it will continue to strengthen the cleaning and management of its public toilets, actively introduce smart technologies and user-friendly amenities, and drive the modernisation of public toilets in terms of both hardware and software to provide a higher-quality environment for residents and visitors. The department also appeals to members of the public and visitors to take good care of public toilet facilities, keep them clean, and work together to safeguard the city's public hygiene.

item.title: Speech by SCST at opening ceremony for Hong Kong Winter Wonderland in Central
item.description:
Following is the speech by the Secretary for Culture, Sports and Tourism, Miss Rosanna Law, at the opening ceremony for Hong Kong Winter Wonderland in Central today (November 18):

     Good evening, everyone, and a very warm welcome.

     It is my great pleasure to be here with you all at the launch ceremony of Hong Kong Winter Wonderland in Central, organised by the Hong Kong Tourism Board to kick off the Hong Kong WinterFest. With Christmas around the corner, Hong Kong, and Central in particular, is already alive with festive excitement, setting the stage to welcome visitors from around the world.

     Following the resounding success of last year's debut of Winter Wonderland and the Immersive Lights Show in Central, the Hong Kong Tourism Board is taking the experience to the next level this year. In addition to Central, we are bringing the Winter Wonderland experience to Tsim Sha Tsui and Causeway Bay, each featuring light shows with distinct themes, so that locals and tourists alike can enjoy this "Only in Hong Kong" experience.  

     Starting tonight and continuing until early January next year, the facades of several iconic landmarks in Central will be illuminated with a spectacular light display, showcasing the sparkling charm of Hong Kong's nightscape. Meanwhile, across Victoria Harbour, Winter Wonderland in Tsim Sha Tsui - also launching later this evening - will offer a complementary winter light experience, creating a dazzling dual attraction alongside the spectacular display in Central.

     Tonight also marks the grand finale of "A Symphony of Lights", which has accompanied us for 22 years. In 2005, "A Symphony of Lights" was recognised by the Guinness World Records as the world's largest permanent light and sound show, and it was among the world's first large-scale light shows performed nightly - showcasing the magnificent night view of Victoria Harbour to countless residents and visitors over the years. The grand finale will feature a rooftop pyrotechnics display, bringing this widely acclaimed show to a perfect close.

     As we have all seen, in recent months, the various promotions and events organised and supported by the Hong Kong Tourism Board - including the International Lantern Spectacular, the Tai Hang Fire Dragon Dance, and the Hong Kong Wine & Dine Festival – have all been very well received by locals and visitors alike. These events have highlighted the city's night-time atmosphere, and we have seen the retail and dining sectors benefit considerably. Looking ahead, the Hong Kong Tourism Board will continue to roll out a wide range of mega events and promotional campaigns. I would like to invite you all - especially those in the travel trade, retail and dining sectors - to join hands with the Hong Kong Tourism Board and work together to enhance Hong Kong's appeal as a night-time tourist destination.

     Christmas is a time of celebration, and I wish all citizens and visitors a joyful holiday season. My heartfelt thanks go to all our guests and partners for your staunch support. Together, we will bring joy and blessings to both locals and visitors this winter.  

     Wish you all a Merry Christmas. Thank you.

item.title: Hong Kong Customs detects two dangerous drugs cases and seizes suspected drugs worth $6.8 million (with photos)
item.description:
Hong Kong Customs detected two dangerous drugs cases on October 27 and yesterday (November 17) and seized about 11 kilograms of suspected ketamine, about 500 grams of suspected etomidate powder, about 2.2kg of suspected liquid etomidate and over 1 300 suspected etomidate capsules. The total estimated market value of the suspected dangerous drug seizures was about $6.8 million. Three persons were arrested.

     In the first case, Hong Kong Customs and anti-smuggling departments of the Mainland Customs conducted a joint operation. Through intelligence exchanges and risk assessment, Customs on October 27 inspected a parcel from the United Kingdom declared as sea salt body scrub sent to Hong Kong via the Mainland. Upon inspection, Customs officers found about 11kg of suspected ketamine in 28 plastic bottles. Upon follow-up investigations, Customs officers conducted a controlled delivery operation and arrested a 50-year-old local female in Jordan yesterday.
     ​
     In the second case, during an anti-narcotics operation conducted in Yuen Long yesterday afternoon, Customs officers intercepted a local male and a Mainland male, both aged 28. Customs officers later escorted them to a nearby residential village for a search and seized the batches of etomidate drug and a batch of suspected drug manufacturing and packaging paraphernalia.

     The arrested woman in the first case has been charged with one count of attempting to traffic in a dangerous drug. The case will be brought up at the Kowloon City Magistrates' Courts tomorrow (November 19).

     The two arrested males in the second case have been jointly charged with one count of manufacture of a dangerous drug and one count of trafficking in a dangerous drug. The arrested local male was also charged with one count of obstructing a member of the Customs and Excise Service. They will appear at the Fanling Magistrates' Courts tomorrow.

     Under the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, manufacture of a dangerous drug and trafficking in a dangerous drug are serious offences. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $5 million and life imprisonment.

     Members of the public may report any suspected drug trafficking activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account  (crimereport@customs.gov.hk) or online form (eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002).

item.title: CE attends opening ceremony of APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen (with photos/videos)
item.description:
The Chief Executive, Mr John Lee, attended the opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit in Shenzhen today (November 18). In bilateral meetings and engagements, he met with leaders of other economies to exchange views on issues of mutual interest.
      
     In the morning, Mr Lee attended the opening ceremony of the APEC CEO Summit. President Xi Jinping attended the opening ceremony and delivered a keynote speech. President Xi pointed out that APEC was born amid the waves of economic globalisation and enabled the Asia-Pacific to steer the course of our times. Noting that this year marks the third time that China has hosted APEC, he said that China is ready to work with all other parties to forge ahead with resolve, jointly build an Asia-Pacific community, and bring prosperity for all in our region. In this connection, President Xi put forward four proposals. First, to uphold peace and stability; second, to build bridges of opening up and co-operation; third, to boost innovation to drive growth; and fourth, that we should expand our ways for mutual benefits and win-win outcomes. President Xi also said that China supports the establishment of a World Association for Bay Areas Economic Cooperation to deepen exchanges and interactions among bay areas from across the world. This will help us explore new ways for stronger economic co-operation in the Asia-Pacific.
      
     Mr Lee said he was deeply encouraged and inspired by President Xi's keynote speech. From a strategic and long-term perspective, the speech charted the course for Asia-Pacific co-operation and profoundly underscored that the more complex the external environment becomes, the more important it is to firmly uphold the post-war international order, persist in resolving differences through dialogue and negotiation, and respond to challenges through solidarity and collaboration, to lay a solid foundation for long-term peace and stability in the Asia-Pacific region. As an APEC member economy, Hong Kong has long served as an important hub for regional economic and trade co-operation and is one of the world's most competitive economies. Hong Kong has consistently supported free trade and multilateralism, and actively leveraged the APEC platform to continuously deepen international exchanges and co-operation.
      
     Afterwards, Mr Lee met with the Prime Minister of Malaysia, Dato' Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said he was pleased to meet him again following the APEC meetings held in Korea in 2025. Mr Lee said that Hong Kong and Malaysia have long enjoyed close co-operation. During his visit to Malaysia in 2023, the two places signed Memoranda of Understanding and agreements covering various areas. With the Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office (ETO) in Kuala Lumpur having officially commenced operation, Hong Kong is further deepening economic and trade ties and investment promotion with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and neighbouring Asian countries. He thanked the Malaysian Government for supporting the establishment of the ETO in Malaysia, and said he looked forward to deeper and broader co-operation between the two places in economic, trade, and people-to-people exchanges. Noting that Hong Kong is developing into an international hub for high-calibre talent and has in recent years actively promoted itself as a Muslim-friendly destination, Mr Lee welcomed more Malaysian students and visitors to Hong Kong.
      
     Mr Lee then met with the President of Vietnam, Mr To Lam. He said he was pleased to meet President To again following his visit to Vietnam in 2024. Mr Lee said that the two places enjoy close economic and trade ties, and that Vietnam is Hong Kong's third-largest trading partner and its largest trading partner among ASEAN member states. Hong Kong announced Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan in September this year, while Vietnam earlier announced its own five-year plan, reflecting the shared vision of both places in promoting high-quality development. He expressed the hope that the two sides would further strengthen government-to-government co-operation and deepen exchanges and collaboration in tourism, people-to-people exchanges and innovation and technology. He encouraged Vietnamese enterprises to make good use of Hong Kong's advantages in connecting the Mainland and the world by using Hong Kong as a springboard to tap into the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and to seize more opportunities together. As Vietnam will be the host of APEC 2027, Hong Kong will work closely with Vietnam to promote regional economic co-operation and integration.
      
     In the afternoon, Mr Lee met with the Sultan of Brunei, Sultan Haji Hassanal Bolkiah. Mr Lee said that, following the APEC meetings held in Korea in 2025, he was pleased to meet the Sultan again. He said that economic and trade co-operation between Hong Kong and Brunei has been progressing steadily, with bilateral merchandise trade increasing by 40 per cent year on year last year. Hong Kong's world-class capital markets, professional services, and aviation and logistics network can provide strong support for deepening co-operation between the two places, and he expressed the hope that both sides would further strengthen collaboration and complement each other's strengths.
      
     Mr Lee later met with the Prime Minister of Thailand, Mr Anutin Charnvirakul. He said he was pleased to meet the Prime Minister again following the APEC meetings held in Korea in 2025. Mr Lee noted that Thailand recently announced a new five-year plan and is actively promoting the development of its innovation and technology industries. As an international innovation and technology centre, Hong Kong is pressing ahead with the development of the Northern Metropolis at full steam, including taking forward such projects as the Northern Metropolis University Town and the Hong Kong Park of the Hetao Shenzhen-Hong Kong Science and Technology Innovation Co-operation Zone, to promote the integrated development of education, technology and talent. Mr Lee expressed the hope that Hong Kong and Thailand would strengthen connectivity and co-operation in innovation and technology, and encouraged more Thai enterprises to establish a presence in Hong Kong to expand into international markets by leveraging Hong Kong's vibrant innovation and technology ecosystem and strong research capabilities.
      
     Mr Lee then met with the President of Chile, Mr José Antonio Kast, and together they witnessed the signing of the Working Holiday Scheme agreement between Hong Kong and Chile. Mr Lee said that Chile is Hong Kong's third-largest trading partner and first Working Holiday Scheme partner in Latin America. The Working Holiday Scheme agreement marks a further extension of exchanges between the two places from economic and trade co-operation to people-to-people and youth levels. It will not only help foster closer ties between the peoples of the two places, but also inject fresh impetus into bilateral relations. The agreement will provide more opportunities for young people of both places to work and engage in cultural exchange and broaden their international horizons, further consolidating and enhancing Hong Kong's role as an international exchange hub. Hong Kong will continue to give full play to its roles as a "super-connector" and "super value-adder", and strengthen co-operation with Chile in different areas.
      
     Mr Lee thanked the leaders of Malaysia, Vietnam, Brunei and Thailand whom he met today for their continued support for Hong Kong's early accession to the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership and joint promotion of regional economic development. He said that in the face of a complex and ever-changing international landscape, Hong Kong is actively expanding into diversified markets, deepening collaboration with ASEAN, Latin America and other countries of the Global South, and further strengthening international exchanges and co-operation. Leveraging Hong Kong's unique advantages of being strongly supported by the motherland and closely connected to the world under the "one country, two systems" principle, the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government is strengthening the development of the "four centres and one hub" to create broader development prospects for enterprises at home and abroad. Hong Kong will continue to strengthen practical co-operation with traditional and emerging markets in such areas as trade and investment, innovation and technology, and people-to-people exchanges, to jointly create more development opportunities.
      
     In the evening, Mr Lee will attend a welcome banquet for participating economies' leaders and representatives.
      
     Mr Lee will attend the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting and meet with leaders of other economies tomorrow (November 19).

item.title: Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Development Office to promote Greater Bay Area entrepreneurial opportunities at Entrepreneur Day

item.title: Import of poultry meat and products from Coagh Townland of Northern Ireland in UK suspended
item.description:
The Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department announced today (November 18) that in view of a notification from the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs of the United Kingdom (UK) about an outbreak of highly pathogenic avian influenza in Coagh Townland of Northern Ireland in the UK, the CFS has instructed the trade to suspend the import of poultry meat and products (including poultry eggs) from the area with immediate effect to protect public health in Hong Kong.
      
     A CFS spokesman said that according to the Census and Statistics Department, Hong Kong imported about 680 tonnes of chilled and frozen poultry meat and about 220 000 poultry eggs from the UK in the first nine months of this year.
      
     "The CFS has contacted the British authority over the issue and will closely monitor information issued by the World Organisation for Animal Health and the relevant authorities on the avian influenza outbreak. Appropriate action will be taken in response to the development of the situation," the spokesman said.

item.title: Hong Kong signs Working Holiday Scheme agreement with Chile (with photos/video)
item.description:
Hong Kong and Chile today (November 18) signed an agreement to mark the establishment of a bilateral Working Holiday Scheme (WHS) for youths of the two places. 

     Witnessed by the Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR), Mr John Lee, and the President of Chile, Mr José Antonio Kast, the WHS agreement was signed by the Secretary for Labour and Welfare of the Government of the HKSAR, Mr Chris Sun, and the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Chile, Mr Francisco Pérez Mackenna, on the sidelines of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting held in Shenzhen.

     Welcoming the establishment of the Scheme with Chile, Mr Sun said, "Chile is Hong Kong's first WHS partner in Latin America. The Scheme will provide young people from Hong Kong and Chile with opportunities to broaden their horizons and gain first-hand experience of living and working in a different cultural environment."

     Mr Pérez Mackenna said, "We are pleased to provide young people from Chile and Hong Kong with new opportunities to experience life in each other's communities. Hong Kong's unique blend of Eastern and Western cultures, international outlook and dynamic economy will offer Chilean youth an enriching experience. We also look forward to welcoming young people from Hong Kong to discover Chile's rich culture, warm hospitality and natural beauty, thereby strengthening mutual understanding and people-to-people ties."

     The Scheme with Chile is Hong Kong's 15th bilateral WHS. Since 2001, Hong Kong has established WHS arrangements with New Zealand, Australia, Ireland, Germany, Japan, Canada, Korea, France, the United Kingdom, Austria, Hungary, Sweden, the Netherlands, and Italy (soon to take effect). So far, over 109 000 Hong Kong youth have benefited from these schemes.

     Under the WHS between Hong Kong and Chile, youths from each side may apply for a visa which will allow them to stay in Chile or Hong Kong for up to 12 months. During the period, they may take temporary jobs to finance their stay or study short-term courses. The annual quota from each side will be 100.

     Details of visa application procedures for applicants from Hong Kong and Chile will be available on the website of the Chilean National Migration Service tramites.extranjeria.gob.cl/ and the website of the Immigration Department of the HKSAR www.immd.gov.hk/ respectively, in due course.

item.title: Government welcomes passage of Banking Legislation (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill 2026
item.description:
The Government welcomed the passage of the Banking Legislation (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill 2026 by the Legislative Council today (November 18). This will enable Hong Kong's banking legislation to keep abreast of the times, better cater for the future development needs of the banking industry, and further align with the regulatory regimes of other major international financial centres.
      
     The Banking Legislation (Miscellaneous Amendments) Ordinance 2026 (Amendment Ordinance) has fully taken into account the operation and regulatory environment of the banking industry in Hong Kong, and has made reference to relevant international standards and practices. The Amendment Ordinance amends the Banking Ordinance in the following areas: (i) regulation of bank holding companies; (ii) engagement of skilled persons for supervisory purposes; (iii) modernisation of enforcement provisions; (iv) simplification of the current three-tier banking system into a two-tier system; and (v) technical amendments to reduce compliance burden and enhance regulatory clarity and effectiveness. The Amendment Ordinance also makes amendments to The Hong Kong Association of Banks Ordinance and the Financial Institutions (Resolution) Ordinance for enhancing operational efficiency and flexibility. 
      
     The Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury, Mr Christopher Hui, said, "The Amendment Ordinance fully demonstrates the Government's steadfast commitment to ensuring that Hong Kong's financial regulatory regime continues to align with international standards, adapts to market changes and keeps pace with the times, thereby providing solid support for the long-term development of the economy and financial markets. The legislative amendments coincide with our work to take forward the First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (2026-2030) and the Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address. We will continue to work closely with the banking industry to build resilient underpinning, uphold stable structures, enhance robust capabilities, and keep risks manageable, so as to jointly consolidate and enhance Hong Kong's international competitive advantages."
      
     The Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, Mr Eddie Yue, said, "A modernised Banking Ordinance is an important prerequisite for a sound and resilient banking system and provides an enabling environment for business development. This round of updates will help ensure the ongoing effectiveness of our regulatory regime, and at the same time place our banking sector in a stronger position to seize new opportunities in the years ahead, thereby reinforcing Hong Kong's status as an international financial centre."
      
     The Amendment Ordinance will come into operation in phases starting from January 1, 2027.

item.title: TCU's second quarterly report of 2026 released
item.description:
The following is issued on behalf of the Transport Advisory Committee:

     The Transport Complaints Unit (TCU) of the Transport Advisory Committee received 12 447 complaints and suggestions in the second quarter of 2026, with 259 being pure suggestions. 

     The complaints and suggestions received during the quarter were mostly related to public transport services (91 per cent), enforcement matters (7 per cent) and traffic conditions (2 per cent).

     The number of cases on public transport services increased from 9 331 in the previous quarter to 11 335 this quarter, while that on illegal parking and other enforcement matters increased from 800 to 836. The number of complaints and suggestions on traffic conditions decreased from 249 to 197 and those on road maintenance decreased from 42 to 40.

     All the complaints and suggestions received by the TCU in the quarter were referred to the relevant government departments and public transport operators for follow-up action.

     During the period under review, investigations into 12 284 cases were completed. Of these, 10 536 cases (86 per cent) were found to be substantiated, six cases (less than 1 per cent) were unsubstantiated, and the remaining 1 742 cases (14 per cent) could not be pursued due to a lack of evidence. 

     For the substantiated cases, the relevant government departments and public transport operators have either taken steps to rectify the situation or are considering possible solutions to the problems identified. Among these cases, nine drivers were summonsed by the Police.

     During the quarter, the relevant government departments and public transport operators took on board 11 suggestions made by the public to enhance public transport services and improve traffic conditions. A summary of the cases is in the Appendix.

     Members of the public may make their suggestions or complaints to the TCU by dialling the hotline 2889 9999 (voice mail service is available outside office hours), by fax to 2577 1858, by email to info@tcu.gov.hk or by filling in a form on the TCU website (www.tcu.gov.hk).

item.title: TAC discusses new bus franchises and fare increase applications from franchised bus operators
item.description:
The following is issued on behalf of the Transport Advisory Committee (TAC):

     With the current franchises of New Lantao Bus Company (1973) Limited (NLB) and the Kowloon Motor Bus Company (1933) Limited (KMB) expiring in March and July 2027 respectively, following the Government's briefing to the Transport Advisory Committee in March 2026 regarding the work associated with the two new franchises upon expiry of the current ones, the TAC was briefed today (November 18) on the latest progress of the Government's negotiation with the relevant franchised bus operators.

     The Chairman of the TAC, Professor Wong Sze-chun, said, "Members noted the Government's work progress to pursue the objective of continuing the provision of efficient and quality public bus service to passengers under the new 10-year franchises. Members welcomed that these two operators have taken on board new commitments to further enhance their services covering four key areas including green initiatives, smart mobility, bus safety and fare concessions, despite the challenging operating environment of the bus industry."

     In addition, the TAC discussed the fare increase applications from operators, including KMB, Citybus Limited, Long Win Bus Company Limited and NLB.

     Professor Wong said the TAC has considered and balanced the basket of factors under the established mechanism when deliberating the fare increase applications from the four operators. These factors include public acceptability and affordability, the service performance of the operators, the past and forecast financial performance of the operators (including the impact of a fuel price upsurge), as well as a supportable fare increase rate computed for reference through a formula taking into account the changes in the Composite Consumer Price Index and the wage index.

     Professor Wong said, "In accordance with the established practice, the TAC will submit its advice on new bus franchises and fare increase applications from franchised bus operators to the Government for consideration by the Chief Executive in Council."

item.title: Speech by SCST at DesignInspire 2026 special tour and networking reception (English only)
item.description:
Following is the speech by the Secretary for Culture, Sports and Tourism, Miss Rosanna Law, at the DesignInspire 2026 special tour and networking reception today (November 18):

Sophia (Executive Director of the Hong Kong Trade Development Council, Ms Sophia Chong), Ambassador Harvey Rouse (Ambassador and Head of Office of the European Union to Hong Kong and Macao), Consul-General Freihofer (Consul General of Switzerland in Hong Kong, Mr Daniel Freihofer), Consul-General Cannito (Consul General of Italy in Hong Kong and Macao, Mr Francesco Paolo Cannito), Steve (Chairman of the Hong Kong Design Centre, Mr Steve Leung), distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen,

     Good afternoon. It is my greatest pleasure to see you all at DesignInspire 2026.

     With the Cultural and Creative Industries Development Agency under my bureau as the lead sponsor, I am delighted to open this year's DesignInspire - an annual flagship international creative exhibition organised by the Hong Kong Trade Development Council and co-organised by the Hong Kong Design Centre. 

     Since its launch in 2017, the DesignInspire has grown into an important meeting place for the global design community. As in past editions, this year's DesignInspire continues to bring together creative talents, businesses, institutions and partners to exchange ideas, develop collaborations and explore new opportunities. With so many bright minds in one place, we are reminded that design is not just about aesthetics - don't get me wrong, it's really important, but also about how design shapes the way we live, how we connect people with places, and how it can inspire us to imagine what comes next, and what should come next.

       Under this year's theme, "Wander & Wonder", and with more than 200 exhibitors from 17 countries and regions, DesignInspire invites us to wander through endless possibilities and immerse ourselves in the wonders created by these design installations. As Sophia said, I have just had a brief tour around some of the major presentations, and I have to say, this is the third DesignInspire event that I have joined in the past two years. This one is by far the most impressive. Thank you very much.

     In particular, I would like to highlight two collaboration projects with Switzerland, our partner country for this year's Business of Design Week, just next door. The first is "Cabinets of Wonders", curated by Chilai Howard, which transforms Switzerland's iconic alpine chalet into an intimate exhibition space for cultural and creative dialogue between Hong Kong and Switzerland. There is a presentation in red and white, featuring the flag of Switzerland of course, but also showing a distinctive Hong Kong element, so watch out for that. The second one, "Breathing in Motion", brought to us by the renowned Swiss design studio Atelier Oï, explores the subtle interactions between body and space, stillness and movement.

     I am also delighted to welcome "ABITO/HK" as it makes its debut at this year's DesignInspire. Presented by Salone del Mobile.Milano in partnership with the Consulate-General of Italy in Hong Kong and Macao, this exhibition places iconic furniture and design pieces from Hong Kong and Italy side by side. It showcases the contrasts - and the similarities - in lifestyles, living spaces and ideas of beauty between the two cultures, revealing distinctive identities and yet shared sensibilities. And if you are a fashion lover, or you are a woman like me, you will feel particularly inspired by the exhibits.

     Another striking exhibition is, of course, curated by our lighting master Tino Kwan and interior designer CM Jao, who are giving their enthralling "House of Lumière" its local debut. It presents selected lighting pieces as works of art, weaving a creative dialogue between light and shadow. And this is one of the places, as Sophia has said, on my next visit to this year's DesignInspire. I will definitely be checking it out in more detail.

     DesignInspire is one of the important projects underpinning the HKSAR (Hong Kong Special Administrative Region) Government's commitment to supporting the development of our cultural and creative industries. In line with Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan and the 2026 Policy Address, we will continue to strengthen Hong Kong's role as an East-meets-West centre for international cultural exchange. Through events like DesignInspire and all other collaborations between the Government and the creative sector, we seek to connect creative talent, encourage new partnerships and help creative businesses thrive.

     My sincere thanks go to the Hong Kong Trade Development Council under Sophia's leadership, the Hong Kong Design Centre with Steve as the Chairman, and all our local and international partners for making DesignInspire possible - and so inspiring.

     I wish DesignInspire 2026 every success, and I wish you all an enjoyable afternoon of discovery and conversation. Thank you.

item.title: Government and industry join hands to develop green maritime fuel trading platform (with photos)
item.description:
The Transport and Logistics Bureau (TLB) said today (November 18) that it has joined hands with the industry to establish the Task Group on the Development of the Green Maritime Fuel Trading Platform. The TLB also signed Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) with industry partners and research organisations to jointly advance Hong Kong's development as a globally oriented, diverse and open green maritime fuel trading centre.

     A spokesman for the TLB said, "Maritime decarbonisation is a global trend, and the International Maritime Organization has set a target for international shipping to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by or around 2050. Among all means of emission reduction, the use of green maritime fuels is by far the most effective, hence the steady increase in their uptake. As trading volumes grow, so does the need for a market to facilitate green maritime fuel transactions.

     "As an international maritime, financial and trading centre, Hong Kong has the unique advantage of being backed by the motherland and having global connectivity, and its financial and legal systems are aligned with international practices. Coupled with the upcoming implementation of the half-rate tax concession for physical trading of eligible commodities, which include green fuels, Hong Kong is well-positioned to establish a market-driven, globally oriented green fuel trading centre, providing a platform that brings together green fuel supplies from the Chinese Mainland and around the world and connects them with demand from the global maritime industry."


     To take this forward, the TLB has joined hands with the industry to establish the Task Group, bringing together energy traders, green fuel producers, maritime and energy industry organisations as well as think tanks to advise on the platform's development directions. The Task Group will also explore the establishment of a Hong Kong green fuel price index based on actual transaction data to provide reliable pricing references for the industry. The Task Group will further advise on building a complete industry chain to support green fuel trading, with a view to helping to attract more stakeholders from the Chinese Mainland and overseas to trade green fuels in Hong Kong.

     Its founding members include the Hydrogen Energy Industry Promotion Association, CIMC Enric Holdings Limited, Hong Kong and China Gas Company Limited, TGT Group Limited, the International Green Fuels Alliance, Our Hong Kong Foundation and AEX Holdings, Ltd.

     To drive the establishment of the trading platform, during Hong Kong Maritime Week, the TLB signed MOUs with multiple partners covering platform development, price index development, solicitation of platform users and industry research, among others.

     Various enterprises and industry organisations spanning green fuel supply, shipping, classification and certification, policy research and financial technology also signed commercial co-operation MOUs on the same day. Through their partnerships, these enterprises and organisations will support the development of the green maritime fuel trading platform.

     The spokesman added, "These collaborations will help to broaden the platform's network of users and partners and promote green fuel trading in Hong Kong. The TLB will continue to work with the industry to advance relevant initiatives and attract more fuel suppliers, shipowners, traders and other stakeholders from the Chinese Mainland and overseas to participate in the green fuel trading platform, thereby strengthening Hong Kong's position as a green maritime fuel bunkering and trading centre."

item.title: Persons in custody at Shek Pik Prison attain good examination results (with photos)
item.description:
​A total of 98 persons in custody (PICs) in Shek Pik Prison (SPP) of the Correctional Services Department (CSD) were presented with certificates at a ceremony today (November 18) in recognition of their study efforts and academic achievements.
      
     In the past year, a total of 284 PICs at SPP passed 522 papers with 258 distinctions and credits in various distance learning courses and public examinations organised by the Hong Kong Metropolitan University (HKMU), the Hong Kong Examinations and Assessment Authority and Caritas Institute of Community Education. The subjects covered Chinese language, English language, mathematics, economics, psychology, sociology, business administration, Putonghua and accounting. The 98 PICs who were awarded certificates today had passed 292 papers with 175 distinctions and credits. Among them, three PICs were awarded Bachelor's Degrees in General Studies, two were awarded Associate Degrees in Business Administration and 10 were awarded Associate Degrees in General Studies by the HKMU.
      
     Officiating at the ceremony, the Vice President of the Hong Kong Shanxi Union Community Limited (HKSUCL), Ms Ng Ching, stated that the HKSUCL has been highly supportive of the rehabilitation work of the CSD, and set up an educational subsidy scheme, namely the HKSUCL - Igniting Hope Education Fund, in 2022 to provide financial assistance to needy PICs for education and vocational training, with a view to facilitating their reintegration into society after release.
      
     During the ceremony, a brass band composed of PICs, alongside volunteer instructors from a local brass ensemble and correctional officers, delivered a joint brass performance. Moreover, singer Jade Kwan and choir instructor Caleb Woo partnered with a band and a choir composed of PICs respectively to perform a selection of uplifting songs. The PICs hoped, through these performances, to express gratitude to their families as well as community members and organisations that have helped them rehabilitate.
      
     In a sharing session, three PICs shared their experiences in the course of rehabilitation and expressed gratitude to their families for their unwavering support. They also thanked correctional officers for their support and encouragement, as well as assistance throughout their learning journeys, enabling them to complete the programmes.
      
     Situated on Lantau Island, SPP is a maximum security institution with a capacity of 426 penal places for male adult PICs.

item.title: HKMC announces successful pricing of HK$22.5 billion multi-currency public benchmark bonds
item.description:
The following is issued on behalf of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority:

     The Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation Limited (HKMC) announced today (November 18) the successful pricing of multi-currency public benchmark bonds totalling HK$22.5 billion (or US$2.87 billion equivalent) (Issuance) under its US$30 billion Medium Term Note Programme. 
      
     Despite volatile interest rate and market conditions, the transaction was successfully book-built and priced in Hong Kong on November 17, 2026. The HKMC adopted a prudent prefunding strategy and maintained proactive communication with both local and international investors to effectively meet its funding needs and advance its core missions. 
      
     The multi-currency benchmark bond issuance with three tranches comprises HK$8 billion 3-year, CNH 5 billion 2-year and US$1.1 billion 5-year bonds. The Issuance attracted strong demand from a diverse group of high-quality local, Southbound Bond Connect and international institutional investors. These included central banks, insurance companies, asset management companies, commercial banks and private banks. The transaction achieved a combined peak orderbook of approximately HK$55 billion equivalent, with final allocations distributed across around 160 accounts. The participation of a broad range of institutional investors underscores the continued support for the HKMC in the debt capital market and the recognition of the HKMC as a high-quality issuer. 
      
     Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer of the HKMC, Mr Colin Pou, said, "This multi-currency bond issuance demonstrates Hong Kong's ability to connect financing needs with local and international capital. Through its public benchmark bond issuance, the HKMC seeks to set pricing benchmarks for potential issuers in the region. Moreover, the offshore Renminbi tranche enriches the array of offshore Renminbi products and deepens financial connectivity between Hong Kong and the Chinese Mainland. These efforts help attract more issuers and investors to Hong Kong and further expand its bond and derivative markets."
      
     The HKMC expresses its sincere gratitude to the Joint Global Coordinators, Joint Bookrunners and Joint Lead Managers, comprising a total of 30 local and international financial institutions, for their professional advice and tremendous support in ensuring the success of the Issuance. The list of participating financial institutions is set out in the Annex.

item.title: Inspection of aquatic products imported from Japan
item.description:
In response to the Japanese Government's plan to discharge nuclear-contaminated water at the Fukushima Nuclear Power Station, the Director of Food and Environmental Hygiene issued a Food Safety Order which prohibits all aquatic products, sea salt and seaweeds originating from the 10 metropolis/prefectures, namely Tokyo, Fukushima, Ibaraki, Miyagi, Chiba, Gunma, Tochigi, Niigata, Nagano and Saitama, from being imported into and supplied in Hong Kong.
 
     For other Japanese aquatic products, sea salt and seaweeds that are not prohibited from being imported into Hong Kong, the Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department is conducting comprehensive radiological tests to verify that the radiation levels of these products do not exceed the guideline levels before they are allowed to be supplied in the market.
 
     From noon on November 17 to noon today (November 18), the CFS conducted tests on the radiological levels of 221 food samples imported from Japan, which were of the "aquatic and related products, seaweeds and sea salt" category. No sample was found to have exceeded the safety limit. Details can be found on the CFS's thematic website titled "Control Measures on Foods Imported from Japan" (www.cfs.gov.hk/english/programme/programme_rafs/programme_rafs_fc_01_30_Nuclear_Event_and_Food_Safety.html).
 
     In parallel, the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) has also tested 50 samples of local catch for radiological levels. All the samples passed the tests. Details can be found on the AFCD's website (www.afcd.gov.hk/english/fisheries/Radiological_testing/Radiological_Test.html).
 
     The Hong Kong Observatory (HKO) has also enhanced the environmental monitoring of the local waters. No anomaly has been detected so far. For details, please refer to the HKO's website (www.hko.gov.hk/en/radiation/monitoring/seawater.html).
 
     From August 24, 2023, to noon today, the CFS and the AFCD have conducted tests on the radiological levels of 276 243 samples of food imported from Japan (including 171 904 samples of aquatic and related products, seaweeds and sea salt) and 58 764 samples of local catch respectively. All the samples passed the tests.

item.title: LCQ7: Financing and digital transformation of small and medium enterprises
item.description:
Following is a question by the Hon Alan Chan and a written reply by the Acting Secretary for Commerce and Economic Development, Dr Bernard Chan, in the Legislative Council today (November 18):
 
Question:
 
     There are views that while Hong Kong is in a period of economic structural transformation, some banks have tightened credit and raised financing thresholds amid the recent decline in market liquidity, leaving micro, small and medium enterprises across various sectors facing difficulties in securing loans, high interest rates and capital chain rupture, which poses a significant challenge to Hong Kong's economic and employment stability. In this connection, will the Government inform this Council:
 
(1) of the respective numbers of applications, amounts approved and latest statistics on default cases/payments under guarantee over the past year in relation to the 80% Guarantee Products and the 90% Guarantee Products under the Special 100% Loan Guarantee;
 
(2) whether the authorities have proactively grasped and assessed the situation regarding banks tightening credit or calling loans for specific sectors (such as catering, retail and wholesale), and what timely countermeasures have been put in place;
 
(3) in the face of a high interest rate environment, whether the authorities and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will explore with major banks in Hong Kong the possibility of further optimising interest rate subsidies, extending repayment grace periods (such as the principal moratorium arrangement), and introducing dedicated concessionary loans for green or digital transformation, so as to alleviate enterprises' cash flow pressure and encourage transformation and upgrading; and
 
(4) regarding the "enhanced Digital Transformation Support Pilot Programme", whether the authorities will collaborate with Cyberport to introduce an official standardised application package (e.g. provision of sector-specific templates), establish dedicated free support teams (e.g. "BEE ePass"), and create a technological solution providers reference list with transparent pricing; if so, of the details and the specific implementation timetable; if not, the reasons for that?
 
Reply:
 
President,
 
     The Government has been promoting the diversified development, upgrading and transformation of small and medium enterprises (SMEs), thereby empowering them to explore new areas of business growth amid the complex and ever-changing market environment while enhancing their market competitiveness.
 
     Having consulted the Innovation, Technology and Industry Bureau, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) and HKMC Insurance Limited (HKMCI), our reply to the various parts of the question is as follows:
 
(1) The Government has been providing loan guarantees through the SME Financing Guarantee Scheme (SFGS) since 2012 to assist the SMEs in obtaining commercial loans. The SFGS is administered and managed by the HKMCI. During the period from November 2025 to October 2026, the application and default figures of the 80% and 90% Guarantee Products under the SFGS are as follows:
 
  80% Guarantee Product
 		 90% Guarantee Product
(The application period ended in end-March 2026)
Number of applications received 3 087 2 612
Number of applications approved 2 657 2 389
Total loan amount of approved applications ($) 8.96 billion 3.95 billion
Number of default cases 286 571
Loan guarantee amount of default cases ($) 0.53 billion 0.56 billion

(2) The HKMA has been paying close attention to the SMEs' lending, by regularly collecting data and maintaining close dialogue with banks, to understand the state of the banking sector's SME lending business. According to the latest data on SME lending collected by the HKMA from banks, the proportion of the SMEs with increased or unchanged credit facility limits has remained broadly stable at consistently over 95 per cent. Based on the HKMA's understanding from banks, the banking sector has been actively supporting corporates' financing needs without tightening underwriting standards.
 
     To deepen understanding of the challenges and needs faced by the SMEs across various sectors, the HKMA has also engaged with different trade associations and their members through various channels and platforms, including the Taskforce on SME Lending (Taskforce) established jointly by the HKMA and the Hong Kong Association of Banks.
 
     Since 2024, the HKMA, together with the banking sector, introduced four rounds of support measures (Note) to assist the SMEs in coping with challenges in their operations. The 18 participating banks in the Taskforce undertook not to demand early repayments from mortgage borrowers who make payments on schedule, and not to adjust credit limits merely due to a decline in the collateral value. For certain cases warranting an adjustment of credit limits, banks will give customers a transition period of at least six months.
 
     At the same time, banks must maintain effective risk management to safeguard depositor interests. For cases of prolonged non-repayment despite relief or restructuring arrangements provided, banks will inevitably take appropriate actions while ensuring such actions are communicated to the customers in an accommodative manner.
 
(3) The banking sector has been actively implementing the multiple rounds of SME support measures and providing credit relief to the SMEs facing short-term cash flow pressure under the overarching principle of prudent risk management. These measures include offering more flexible repayment arrangements, such as extending the duration of partial principal repayment, providing more options on the proportion and duration of partial principal repayment, or even offering principal moratorium arrangement.
 
     Furthermore, the 18 participating banks in the Taskforce have set aside a total of over $450 billion of dedicated funds for the SMEs in their loan portfolios. They have also introduced more diverse products and services to assist the SMEs in their business expansion as well as digital, intelligent and green transformation. The HKMA and the banking sector will continue to closely monitor market developments to understand the needs of the SMEs in different sectors and provide suitable support for the SMEs' continuous development and transformation.
 
(4) The Government and Cyberport are actively preparing for the launch of the enhanced Digital Transformation Support Pilot Programme (DTSPP 2.0) to support eligible SMEs of all industries in adopting off-the-shelf basic AI solutions. Cyberport has established a dedicated team to oversee the implementation of DTSPP 2.0.
 
     To simplify the application and vetting procedures, Cyberport will upgrade the electronic application system by introducing technologies such as AI, automated workflows and data analytics to assist in document data extraction and verification processes, thereby reducing manual handling while streamlining procedures and enhancing vetting accuracy and efficiency. The enhanced system will also include automatic notification function to help the SMEs supplement missing information or confirm their eligibility at an early stage during application submission, thereby reducing delays caused by incomplete applications. The DTSPP 2.0 will also interface with the Government's Digital Corporate Identity (CorpID), requiring both the SMEs and solution providers to complete digital identity authentication through the CorpID, thereby reducing the administrative burden on the SMEs.
 
     To enhance information transparency, Cyberport will help the SMEs grasp the application requirements through briefing sessions, solution showcase days, thematic website and customer support services, as well as helping them select suitable solutions through a simple online self-assessment tool. Solution providers under the DTSPP 2.0 are required to register in advance and their qualifications, service capabilities, solution features, price reasonableness and implementation arrangements must be comprehensively assessed by Cyberport to ensure compliance with the requirements of the Programme. Cyberport will also publicly display the approved solutions and their prices on the website to ensure market transparency, enabling the SMEs to adopt affordable, user-friendly and readily implementable off-the-shelf basic AI solutions.
 
Note: The HKMA and the banking sector introduced nine measures and five measures in March 2024 and October 2024 respectively to support the SMEs in accessing financing, and their continuous development, upgrade and transformation. Additional sector-specific measures were introduced in April 2025 and a new round of measures to assist the SMEs affected by oil price volatility was launched in April 2026.
